docs.title: Project Territory
docs.text:
These pages are the actions your script can use. Each one says where it runs, what you give it, what you get back, and shows a short example.

How to install a resource stays in that resource's README.md. Do not open another resource's database tables yourself. Use the action on its page.

docs.title: Words used here
docs.text:
• Server — the computer running the game. Players do not see this code.
  • Player's game — RedM on their computer. Some actions only work there.
  • Call — an action another script can use. It looks like exports.fw_core:IsReady().
  • Player number — written as source. The server gives each connected player a number. That number changes every time they join.
  • Nothing — written as nil. The call did not find what you asked for.
  • Message — written as an event. Your script hears it only if it is already running. If your script starts later, you missed it.

docs.title: Start order
docs.text:
ensure oxmysql
ensure vorp_lib
ensure fw_core
ensure fw_menu
ensure fw_admin
ensure fw_characters
ensure fw_creator
ensure fw_clothing
ensure fw_inventory
ensure fw_money
ensure fw_weapons
ensure fw_satchel
ensure fw_stores
ensure fw_trade
ensure fw_guide

The folder resources/[framework]/ is only a category. The resource name is the directory name, such as fw_core.

docs.title: What each resource is for
docs.text:
Resource You use it to vorp_lib Show the loading prompt, the revolver cylinder at the bottom right. Put a blip on the map, and a card on that blip. fw_core Read the connected account, and check in that your script was written for the current set of calls. fw_menu Open a menu on the player's screen. fw_admin Check that a player is an in-game admin, and open the admin menu. fw_characters Create, read, select, and save a character. fw_creator See how the character menu stores a body and hair. Other resources should call fw_characters. fw_clothing Read or replace the clothes the character is wearing, and toggle a piece on their body. fw_inventory Give items, open a chest or pouch, and define item types. fw_money Read, give, and take the dollars a character is carrying. fw_weapons Read the equipped guns and tools, or move one between the bag and a slot. fw_satchel The bag screen. It has no calls of its own. fw_stores Open a store counter and settle a purchase into the bag. fw_trade Trade with a nearby player, or give them one item. fw_guide Open the help screen. Database See which id to store on your own table.

fw_core creates the account when a player connects. fw_characters creates the character when something calls CreateCharacter. The character menu does that for players. fw_clothing saves worn clothes on that character. fw_inventory saves the satchel. fw_money saves the dollars that character is carrying. fw_weapons saves the equipped kit. fw_satchel is the screen. fw_stores is the store counter. fw_trade is two players trading what is in those satchels. fw_guide is the help screen.

Cash is fw_money. A bank and jobs are not here yet. Store fw_characters.id for something that belongs to one character, and fw_players.id for something that belongs to the account.

What you get back is a snapshot. Changing it does not save. Use the call that writes that field.

docs.title: Write a script
docs.text:
Wait until fw_core is ready, then check in with RegisterResource(1).

The check-in is how your script says "I was written for the current set of calls." Right now that set is number 1. You do not pick a version, and you do not pass your script's name. If a later update changes the calls so an old script would break, the server window tells you to update yours, instead of failing in the middle of someone's visit. fw_core explains this in full. The other calls still work if you skip it. Do it anyway.

The server can say fw_core has started while it is still creating the player list. If you ask once and stop, you asked too soon. Keep asking for about two minutes.

CreateThread(function()
    local timeoutAt = GetGameTimer() + 120000
    while not exports.fw_core:IsReady() do
        if GetGameTimer() >= timeoutAt then
            print('[my_resource] fw_core is not ready')
            return
        end
        Wait(100)
    end

    local ok, err = exports.fw_core:RegisterResource(1)
    if not ok then
        print('[my_resource] ' .. tostring(err))
        return
    end
end)

AddEventHandler('fw_core:playerLoaded', function(source, player)
    print(('source %d is account %d'):format(source, player.id))
end)

Put RegisterResource in your own script. You do not type your script's name. The server already knows who called.

fw_core:playerLoaded is a message on the server. It is not sent to the player's game. Your script hears it only if it is already running. If the player joined before your script started, ask GetPlayer instead.

docs.title: A good start looks like this
docs.text:
[fw_core][info] ready version=1.1.0 api=1
[fw_admin] ready
[fw_characters][info] ready version=1.0.0
[fw_creator] ready
[fw_clothing] ready. Purchases are not charged yet. Cash is fw_money.
[fw_inventory] ready. 5 items.

In the server console, fw_health and fw_characters print status. A player who types them gets nothing.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Do not read or write these tables from your script. Use the call on the matching page. This page tells you which id to save on a table you own, and what the columns mean when a call gives you a snapshot.

The database name in server.cfg is TerritoryFRP. If it does not exist yet, oxmysql creates it and connects again. The name can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores. Replacing oxmysql with an untouched copy removes that auto-create. The framework still creates the tables below when each resource starts.

If a table already exists and is missing the column that resource expects, the resource logs the mismatch and does not change the table. fw_items is the exception: missing weapon, item_group, kit, and hash columns are added, and a leftover image column from an older version is dropped.

Do not put money or jobs on these tables. A later resource adds its own table and stores a character id or an account id. See A table of your own.

docs.title: fw_players
docs.text:
Created by fw_core. One row per Rockstar license. There is no call yet to change role, warnings, slots, or bans. Change those in the table. They are read the next time that person joins.

Schema

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_players` (
  `id` int unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `license` varchar(64) NOT NULL,
  `steam` varchar(40) DEFAULT NULL,
  `discord` varchar(40) DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `role` varchar(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',
  `character_slots` tinyint unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
  `warnings` smallint unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `banned` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `banned_until` int unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `created_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `last_seen` timestamp NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `uq_fw_players_license` (`license`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

Columns

Column Lua field Written when Meaning id id Insert Account id. Store this on child tables. license license Insert license:… or license2:…, prefix included. Unique. Max 64 bytes. steam steam Every successful admit steam:… up to 40 bytes, or NULL. discord discord Every successful admit discord:… up to 40 bytes, or NULL. name name Every successful admit Display name, clipped to 64 characters. role role Default 'user' on insert Account role. Not a job. Read into memory at connect. The creator's ped permission and admin commands use it. character_slots characterSlots Default 5 on insert Max characters for this account. CreateCharacter re-reads this column at create time. warnings warnings Default 0 Stored only. No enforcement. banned banned Checked at connect 1 refuses the connection. A connected player's in-memory copy shows false, because a banned license never attaches. banned_until bannedUntil Checked at connect Unix time. 0 with banned = 1 means the ban does not expire. A time in the past clears banned on the next connect. created_at — Insert Not included on the Lua player record. last_seen — Admit, and again on drop Not included on the Lua player record.

Indexes: primary key id, unique license. Lookups by steam or discord are not indexed — add one if a feature queries those columns.

Relationships: ON DELETE CASCADE from fw_characters.player_id — deleting an account deletes its characters.

Calls: fw_core. The fields you get back are the account.

docs.title: fw_characters
docs.text:
Created by fw_characters. One row per character. Do not change this table from another script. Use the calls on fw_characters.

Schema

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_characters` (
  `id` int unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `player_id` int unsigned NOT NULL,
  `slot` tinyint unsigned NOT NULL,
  `first_name` varchar(50) NOT NULL,
  `last_name` varchar(50) NOT NULL,
  `nickname` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `gender` enum('male','female') NOT NULL,
  `birth_date` date DEFAULT NULL,
  `description` text NOT NULL,
  `appearance` json DEFAULT NULL,
  `clothing` json DEFAULT NULL,
  `barber` json DEFAULT NULL,
  `x` float NOT NULL,
  `y` float NOT NULL,
  `z` float NOT NULL,
  `heading` float NOT NULL,
  `health` smallint unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 600,
  `health_core` tinyint unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
  `stamina_core` tinyint unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
  `is_dead` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `created_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `last_played` timestamp NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `uq_fw_characters_player_slot` (`player_id`, `slot`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_fw_characters_player`
    FOREIGN KEY (`player_id`) REFERENCES `fw_players` (`id`)
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC;

Columns

Column Lua field Meaning id id Character id. The id inventory, money, and jobs should store later. player_id playerId Owner. fw_players.id. slot slot 1 through that account's character_slots. Unique per account. Deleting a character frees the slot. Omitting slot on create uses the lowest free one. first_name firstName 1–50 characters. last_name lastName 1–50 characters. nickname nickname NULL when unset. gender gender male or female. birth_date birthDate YYYY-MM-DD or NULL. Year must sit in FwCharactersConfig (1800–1899). description description Lore, up to 2000 characters. Always sent on insert, including ''. appearance appearance Body and face JSON. NULL until SetAppearance. The creator stores the menu ped-data table here. clothing clothing Worn clothes, outfits, and wearable state. NULL until fw_clothing saves it. The shape is on fw_clothing. barber barber Hair, overlays, and presets. The shape is on fw_creator. x, y, z x, y, z Last position. Insert uses defaultSpawn; the creator then saves the chosen spawn. While the character is online, a newer sample lives in the fw_characters server cache and is what a reconnect reads until the cache is flushed into these columns. heading heading Degrees. health health 0–65535. Default 600. health_core healthCore 0–100. Default 100. stamina_core staminaCore 0–100. Default 100. is_dead isDead 0 or 1. Lua uses true / false. created_at createdAt Insert time. last_played lastPlayed Select, clear, or player drop. NULL until the first selection.

Indexes: primary key id, unique (player_id, slot) — listing one account uses this index. The JSON columns are not indexed. ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC keeps a large document off the main row.

Write paths: SaveState updates position and health only — it never rewrites appearance, clothing, or barber. Each of those documents must encode to at most 262144 bytes. GetCharacters never selects the JSON columns; it selects (appearance IS NOT NULL) AS has_appearance (and the same for clothing/barber) and returns those as hasAppearance, hasClothing, hasBarber.

Calls: fw_characters. The fields you get back are the character record.

docs.title: A table of your own
docs.text:
A resource that stores something for a character should follow this shape:

  • Its own table, created by that resource.
  • A column character_id that stores fw_characters.id.
  • A foreign key to fw_characters(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE when the data must disappear with the character.
  • No copy of the character's name, gender, or appearance — read those through exports.fw_characters.

An account-level table uses player_id → fw_players.id the same way.

The character id to use is the one from CreateCharacter, GetActiveCharacter, or Player(source).state.fwCharacterId. The account id is player.id from GetPlayer, or Player(source).state.fwPlayerId.

docs.title: fw_inventory
docs.text:
Created by fw_inventory from resources/[framework]/fw_inventory/sql/inventory.sql. One row per character. The grid document and the item fields are in fw_inventory.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_inventory` (
  `character_id` int unsigned NOT NULL,
  `grid` json NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`character_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_fw_inventory_character`
    FOREIGN KEY (`character_id`) REFERENCES `fw_characters` (`id`)
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC;
Column Meaning character_id fw_characters.id. Primary key. Deleting the character deletes the row. grid JSON document: width, height, baseWidth, baseHeight, bonus, nextId, and items. At most 262144 bytes. width and height are the drawn size. updated_at Set by the database when the row is written.

docs.title: fw_items
docs.text:
Created by fw_inventory from resources/[framework]/fw_inventory/sql/items.sql. One row per item type. This is not a satchel. Placements stay in fw_inventory.grid.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_items` (
  `name` varchar(32) NOT NULL,
  `label` varchar(48) NOT NULL,
  `description` varchar(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `width` tinyint unsigned NOT NULL,
  `height` tinyint unsigned NOT NULL,
  `stack` smallint unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `weapon` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `item_group` varchar(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `rotate` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `kit` varchar(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `hash` varchar(48) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (`name`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
Column Meaning name Primary key. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. The name AddItem uses. label Satchel text. description Side panel. width, height Cell footprint before turning. stack Copies that share one footprint. 1 means each copy is placed on its own. weapon 1 when the item never stacks. A weapon is always one placement. item_group Filter and sort group. ammo, animals, documents, food, herbs, horse, medical, tools, valuables, currency, weapons, materials, or container. rotate 1 when the player can turn it. kit Set only on a weapon item. Which equip slot it fills: lasso, binoculars, lantern, bow, revolver, pistol, longarm, melee, or fishingrod. Empty string on a non-weapon item. hash Set only on a weapon item. The game's weapon name, such as WEAPON_REVOLVER_CATTLEMAN. Empty string on a non-weapon item.

An older version of this table had an image column instead of kit and hash. That column is dropped on start if it is still there. The picture is fw_inventory/images/<name>.png. An item file can set image to another name in that folder, such as bill_stack_single for dollars. That name stays on the item file. It is not a column. rarity and mission stay on the item file too, and they are copied back when the files load. Files in items/ are written into this table on start and on fw_items_reload. A row inserted for an admin tool stays until it is deleted. The field list and the insert example are in fw_inventory. The container block on a pouch is not a column. It stays on the item file and is merged back onto the catalog when the files load.

docs.title: fw_storage
docs.text:
Created by fw_inventory from resources/[framework]/fw_inventory/sql/storage.sql. One row per chest, wagon, horse, or container item. The id is chosen by the caller. Opening and moving items is in fw_inventory.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_storage` (
  `id` varchar(64) NOT NULL,
  `grid` json NOT NULL,
  `groups` json NULL,
  `updated_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC;
Column Meaning id Caller id, such as chest:valentine_1 or item: plus a container id. grid Same document shape as a satchel: width, height, baseWidth, baseHeight, and items. At most 262144 bytes. groups JSON list of item groups this row accepts. NULL accepts every group. updated_at Set by the database when the row is written.

docs.title: fw_currency
docs.text:
Created by fw_money from resources/[framework]/fw_money/sql/currency.sql. One row per character and currency name. This is the dollars that character is carrying in the satchel. Do not write this table from your script. Use fw_money.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_currency` (
  `character_id` int unsigned NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  `amount` int unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (`character_id`, `name`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_fw_currency_character`
    FOREIGN KEY (`character_id`) REFERENCES `fw_characters` (`id`)
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
Column Meaning character_id fw_characters.id. Deleting the character deletes the row. name Currency name. cash is dollars. amount Whole dollars this character can spend. That is loose piles in the satchel, plus piles inside a pouch still in the satchel. Each pile holds at most 500.

docs.title: fw_storage_currency
docs.text:
Created by fw_money from resources/[framework]/fw_money/sql/storage_currency.sql. One row per storage id and currency name. This is the dollars inside a chest, or inside a pouch that is on the ground. A pouch still in the satchel does not keep a row. Those dollars stay on fw_currency. The row is removed when the amount returns to 0, and when that storage is deleted. Do not write this table from your script.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_storage_currency` (
  `storage_id` varchar(64) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  `amount` int unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (`storage_id`, `name`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
Column Meaning storage_id The storage id from fw_storage, such as item: plus a container id, or a chest id. name Currency name. cash is dollars. amount Whole dollars in that storage.

docs.title: fw_weapons
docs.text:
Created by fw_weapons from resources/[framework]/fw_weapons/sql/weapons.sql. One row per character. Do not write this table from your script. Read and change the kit with fw_weapons.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `fw_weapons` (
  `character_id` int unsigned NOT NULL,
  `kit` json NOT NULL,
  `ammo` json NULL,
  `updated_at` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`character_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_fw_weapons_character`
    FOREIGN KEY (`character_id`) REFERENCES `fw_characters` (`id`)
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC;
Column Meaning character_id fw_characters.id. Deleting the character deletes the row. kit The equipped slots. Read them with GetKit. ammo How many rounds of each kind are on the character. fw_weapons writes this when the player uses a box or fires. updated_at Set by the database when the row is written.

docs.title: fw_admin
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Ask this before you do something only an admin should do.

An admin is a player named in permissions.cfg. Being able to open the txAdmin website does not make them an admin. Setting their account label to admin in the database does not make them an admin either.

add_ace group.admin fw.admin allow
add_principal identifier.license:YOUR_LICENSE group.admin

server.cfg loads that file with the line exec permissions.cfg. After you edit it, restart the server, or type exec permissions.cfg in the server window. fw_admin reads permissions.cfg again on every check, so a player who is already in the game picks up the change right away. They do not have to leave and join again.

fw.admin passes every admin check, including a smaller one such as fw.admin.kick. A helper who should only kick gets that smaller permission, and does not get fw.admin.

Type fw_admin and a player number in the server window. It writes INFO lines with that player's ids so you can copy the license: line.

docs.title: IsReady
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Says yes once fw_admin has finished starting: fw_core answered its own IsReady as yes, and fw_admin checked in with it.

You do not need to wait for this before calling IsAdmin or HasPermission. Those two already work as soon as fw_admin starts, even in the moment it is still waiting on fw_core underneath. IsReady is here for a script that only wants to confirm fw_admin itself started cleanly, for example after seeing [fw_admin] ready in the server window.

--- True once fw_admin has finished starting.
---@return boolean ready
exports.fw_admin:IsReady()

docs.title: IsAdmin
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes for the server window, and yes for a player who has fw.admin. No for everyone else, and no if you pass something that is not a real player number.

--- True when this player may use admin tools.
---@param source integer player number, or 0 for the server window
---@return boolean
exports.fw_admin:IsAdmin(source)

source is the player's number for this visit. Use 0 when the check is for the server window itself, not a player.

if not exports.fw_admin:IsAdmin(source) then
    return
end

docs.title: HasPermission
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes when the player has fw.admin, or has the one smaller permission you name. A permission that does not start with fw.admin. is always no — this will not answer questions about any other server permission, admin or not.

--- True when the player has fw.admin, or the smaller permission you pass.
---@param source integer player number, or 0 for the server window
---@param permission string|nil such as 'fw.admin.kick'
---@return boolean
exports.fw_admin:HasPermission(source, permission)

The server window passes any fw.admin. permission you name. A player who only has fw.admin.kick passes this check for that name, and IsAdmin is still no for them.

if not exports.fw_admin:HasPermission(source, 'fw.admin.kick') then
    return
end

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Who What happens /admin A player in the game Opens the admin menu when they have fw.admin. Anyone else gets a log line saying they are not an admin. /tpm A player in the game Moves them to the waypoint on their map when they have fw.admin. Anyone else gets a log line saying they are not an admin. Set a waypoint first. If the ground under it cannot be found, the log says so and they stay where they are. /fw_admin The player who types it The log says whether they are an admin. It does not print their ids. fw_admin Server window Prints whether fw_admin is ready. fw_admin <serverId> Server window Prints whether that player is an admin, and their ids, so you can copy the license: line into permissions.cfg. admin (no slash) Server window Prints that /admin is for a player in the game. It does nothing else. tpm Server window Prints that /tpm is for a player in the game. It does nothing else.

/admin opens a menu from fw_menu. It needs fw.admin. A smaller permission such as fw.admin.kick does not open it.

The first page has three entries.

  • Players. Who is online. Search filters that list. Unban asks for a license. Choose a person, then go to them, bring them, send them back, watch them, freeze them, fill their health, revive them, give an item, give dollars, kick, or ban.
  • Self. God mode, no clip, invisible, infinite ammo, fill health, fill health and stamina, and revive. No clip moves with W and S, up with Q, down with Z. Shift changes the speed. Delete stops it.
  • Developer tools. Teleports, then copy coordinates. Teleports are the map waypoint, coordinates you type, Guarma, and the trip back. TP to Waypoint is the same move as /tpm. Copy coordinates puts x y z, a vector3, a vector4, or the heading on the clipboard. The same line is also written to the F8 log. The clipboard call is exports.vorp_lib:copyToClipBoard. If vorp_lib is not started, nothing is copied and the log says the clipboard is not available.

Go back on a page returns to the page that opened it.

Giving an item uses fw_inventory AddItem. The count is from 1 to 500. Giving dollars uses fw_money AddCash. The amount is from 1 to 100000. Both land in the satchel of the character they are playing. If that character is not selected, or the satchel has no room, nothing is given and the log says why.

A ban asks for the hours. 0 does not expire. The longest timed ban from the menu is 8760 hours, which is one year. The menu saves it with fw_core SetBan, then removes them from the server. Unban asks for the license, including license: at the front. A hex id on its own is treated as a Rockstar license.

Bring remembers where that person was standing, on the server. Send back uses that spot. A second bring keeps the first spot. Guarma remembers where you were standing the same way. If there is no remembered spot, back from Guarma uses a mainland spot near Saint Denis.

The server checks the permission again before it does the thing. A menu left open by someone who loses admin will not let them teleport, kick, or give.

docs.title: Smaller permissions
docs.text:
fw.admin passes every check below. Give a helper only the line they should have. They still cannot open /admin without fw.admin. The check matters when their game asks the server directly.

Permission What it allows fw.admin.players The player list, go to, bring, send back, freeze, fill health, revive, and spectate. fw.admin.kick Kick. fw.admin.ban Ban and unban. fw.admin.give Give an item, or give dollars.

Self tools, the waypoint, typed coordinates, Guarma, and copy coordinates need fw.admin.

add_ace group.helper fw.admin.kick allow
add_principal identifier.license:YOUR_LICENSE group.helper

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
These are networked events, sent with RegisterNetEvent and TriggerServerEvent / TriggerClientEvent — not AddEventHandler. None of them are queued: the listening side has to already be running when the message is sent, or it is simply missed. fw_admin's own client and server scripts are always running together while the resource is started, so this mostly matters if your own script triggers one of them.

A new admin tool should check IsAdmin or HasPermission itself first, then do its own work. Prefer AddItem, AddCash, and SetBan when you are giving or banning from your own script. The events below belong to the menu. The server ignores an ask when the permission is no.

You can open the same menu from your own server script:

if not exports.fw_admin:IsAdmin(source) then
    return
end
TriggerClientEvent('fw_admin:openMenu', source)

docs.title: fw_admin:openMenu
docs.text:
Networked, server to the player's game. Opens the admin menu for that player. Their game shows "The menu is not running." in the log instead if fw_menu is not started.

--- Networked. Trigger this from the server once you have already checked IsAdmin.
---@param source integer the player to open the menu for
TriggerClientEvent('fw_admin:openMenu', source)

docs.title: fw_admin:log
docs.text:
Networked, server to that player's game. The menu writes the same line in the server window and in their F8 log. level is info, warn, or error.

--- Networked. Sent by fw_admin with a line for that player's F8 log.
---@param message string
---@param level string|nil
TriggerClientEvent('fw_admin:log', source, message, level)

docs.title: Asks from the menu
docs.text:
Networked, the player's game to the server. target is the other player's number for this visit. The server reads where people are standing itself. Send back cannot be aimed at a spot the game invented.

Event Permission Arguments fw_admin:requestPlayers fw.admin.players None. The reply is fw_admin:playerList. fw_admin:goTo fw.admin.players target fw_admin:bring fw.admin.players target fw_admin:sendBack fw.admin.players target fw_admin:freeze fw.admin.players target. Choose it again to let them move. fw_admin:heal fw.admin.players target, stamina. stamina true also fills stamina. fw_admin:revive fw.admin.players target fw_admin:spectate fw.admin.players target. The same target again stops it. fw_admin:spectateLost fw.admin None. Their game sends this when the person can no longer be watched. fw_admin:kick fw.admin.kick target fw_admin:ban fw.admin.ban target, hours. 0 does not expire. fw_admin:unban fw.admin.ban license fw_admin:giveItem fw.admin.give target, name, count fw_admin:giveCash fw.admin.give target, amount fw_admin:self fw.admin tool, and sometimes false to force it off. tool is god, noclip, invis, ammo, heal, stamina, or revive. fw_admin:teleportWaypoint fw.admin None. fw_admin:teleportCoords fw.admin x, y, z fw_admin:teleportGuarma fw.admin None. fw_admin:teleportReturn fw.admin None. fw_admin:copyCoords fw.admin kind: xyz, vector3, vector4, or heading.

docs.text:
Networked, server to one player. The menu sends these after the check. Another script should not trigger them. If you need to move, give, or ban, do that in your own script with your own check.

Event Who receives it Arguments fw_admin:playerList The admin A list of { id, name }, or false when they may not see it. fw_admin:doMove The player who is moving x, y, z, heading fw_admin:doFreeze The player being frozen toggle fw_admin:doHeal The player being healed stamina fw_admin:doRevive The player being revived None fw_admin:doSpectate The admin target, or 0 to stop fw_admin:doSelf The admin tool, on fw_admin:doTeleportWaypoint The admin None fw_admin:doCopy The admin kind 
--- Networked. Sent by the server after a player action it allowed.
---@param x number
---@param y number
---@param z number
---@param heading number|nil
TriggerClientEvent('fw_admin:doMove', source, x, y, z, heading)

docs.title: fw_admin:teleportWaypoint
docs.text:
Networked, player's game to the server. Asks to teleport that player to their own map waypoint. The server ignores it unless IsAdmin is yes for whoever sent it. The admin menu sends this itself. /tpm checks fw.admin and then does the same move.

--- Networked. Sent by the admin menu. The server ignores it unless IsAdmin is yes for the sender.
TriggerServerEvent('fw_admin:teleportWaypoint')

docs.title: fw_admin:doTeleportWaypoint
docs.text:
Networked, server to the player's game. Moves that player to their own map waypoint. It is sent back automatically after a fw_admin:teleportWaypoint from an admin. If that player has no waypoint set, or the ground under it cannot be found, their F8 log says so and nothing moves.

--- Networked. Sent automatically by fw_admin after a valid fw_admin:teleportWaypoint.
---@param source integer the player to move
TriggerClientEvent('fw_admin:doTeleportWaypoint', source)

docs.title: State bags
docs.text: This resource does not set one.

docs.title: fw_characters
docs.text:
Runs on the server. This is how you create a character, read one, and save where they are standing or a saved document on them. Do not write the fw_characters table yourself.

This does not open the character menu, and it does not move the player. The character menu does those things, then uses the calls on this page. Your script should use these calls too.

Ask IsReady first. If it says no, every other call on this page comes back empty, and the reason is fw_characters is not ready. nil on this page means nothing came back.

A call that takes a character id checks that this player owns that character. A missing character and someone else's character both come back as character not found.

What you get back is a snapshot. Changing it does not save. Use UpdateCharacter, SetAppearance, SetClothing, SetBarber, or SaveState.

docs.title: IsReady
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes after startup has finished.

--- True when character calls can be used.
---@return boolean ready
exports.fw_characters:IsReady()

docs.title: GetCharacters
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Every character on this player's account, lowest slot first. The body, clothes, and hair are left out. hasAppearance, hasClothing, and hasBarber say whether each one was saved.

--- The character list for this player, or nil when the player is not in the server.
---@param source integer
---@return table[]|nil characters
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:GetCharacters(source)

source is the player's number for this visit. player is not loaded means that player has not finished joining.

local list, err = exports.fw_characters:GetCharacters(source)
if list == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

for index = 1, #list do
    local character = list[index]
    print(character.id, character.firstName, character.hasAppearance)
end

docs.title: GetCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. One full character, including body, clothes, and hair, when this player owns it.

--- One character owned by this player, or nil and a reason.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@return table|nil character
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:GetCharacter(source, characterId)
err When player is not loaded That player has not finished joining. character id must be a positive integer The id is missing or below 1. character not found No character with that id on this account. 
local character, err = exports.fw_characters:GetCharacter(source, characterId)
if character == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: GetActiveCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The character this player is playing right now. You get nothing, and no reason, when nobody is selected. You get nothing and a reason when this resource is not ready yet.

--- The character selected for this player.
--- Nil when no character is selected.
---@param source integer
---@return table|nil character
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:GetActiveCharacter(source)

local character, err = exports.fw_characters:GetActiveCharacter(source)
if character == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

Ask this again when you need a fresh copy. Do not keep the old one and treat it as live.

docs.title: CreateCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Creates a character and gives you the new id. It does not make that character the one they are playing. Use SelectCharacter for that.

Position and health on the new row come from the character config, not from data. The menu saves the spawn the player picked with SaveState right after.

--- Creates a character and returns the new id.
--- Nil and a reason when the name, gender, slot, or document is rejected.
---@param source integer
---@param data table
---@return integer|nil characterId
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:CreateCharacter(source, data)
Field Required Rule firstName yes 1–50 characters. lastName yes Same as the first name. gender yes male or female. Male is accepted and stored in lowercase. birthDate no YYYY-MM-DD between the configured years, or leave it out. '' stores nothing. nickname no 1–50 characters, or '' to store nothing. description no Up to 2000 characters. Leave it out and it is stored as empty. slot no A free slot from 1 through this account's character limit. Leave it out and the lowest free slot is used. appearance, clothing, barber no A table, or leave it out. The saved text cannot be larger than 262144 bytes. err When player is not loaded That player has not finished joining. character data must be a table data is not a table. first name must be text The name is not text. The same shape is used for the last name, nickname, and description. first name contains unsupported characters The name has a control character. first name must be 1 to 50 characters Empty or too long. Description uses 2000. gender must be male or female Missing or any other value. birth date must be YYYY-MM-DD Present and not that shape. birth date must be a real date from 1800 to 1899 Outside the configured years, or not a real day. appearance must be a table Present and not a table. The same words are used for clothing and barber. could not encode appearance The table could not be saved as text. appearance is too large Over 262144 bytes. character slot limit reached This account already has as many characters as it is allowed. character slot is not available That slot is taken or out of range. could not create the character The insert failed. 
local characterId, err = exports.fw_characters:CreateCharacter(source, {
    firstName = 'Jane',
    lastName = 'Doe',
    gender = 'female',
    birthDate = '1870-04-12',
})
if characterId == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

local selected, selectErr = exports.fw_characters:SelectCharacter(source, characterId)
if not selected then
    print(selectErr)
end

After a successful insert, the local event fw_characters:created fires with the new character. It is not selected yet.

docs.title: UpdateCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Changes name, gender, nickname, birth date, or description. Fields you leave out stay as they are. This does not change body, clothes, hair, position, or health.

--- Updates identity fields that are present in data.
--- Nil and a reason when there is nothing to update or the character is not owned.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@param data table
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:UpdateCharacter(source, characterId, data)

'' for nickname or birth date clears that field. '' for description stores an empty description.

nothing to update means data had none of those fields. character not found means this player does not own that id.

The local event fw_characters:updated fires with the source and the character id. It does not include the new values. Call GetCharacter.

docs.title: SelectCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Makes this character the one the player is playing. It does not move them. Your script does that, using x, y, z, and heading from the character you get back.

--- Selects an owned character for this player.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:SelectCharacter(source, characterId)

character not found means this player does not own that id. Selecting the character they are already playing returns true and fires nothing. Selecting a different one fires fw_characters:cleared for the old id, then fw_characters:selected with a copy of the new character.

docs.title: ClearCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The player is no longer playing a character. True when it cleared one, and true when none was selected. player is not loaded when source is not a player id.

--- Clears the character selected for this player.
---@param source integer
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:ClearCharacter(source)

fw_characters:cleared fires only when a character was actually selected. The player's game also receives fw_characters:released for that same character.

docs.title: SetAppearance, SetClothing, SetBarber
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Replaces one saved block on a character this player owns. Pass nothing (nil) to clear it. The same rules apply to all three calls.

--- Replaces the body document. Nil clears it.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@param value table|nil
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:SetAppearance(source, characterId, value)

--- Replaces the clothing document. Nil clears it.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@param value table|nil
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:SetClothing(source, characterId, value)

--- Replaces the hair and makeup document. Nil clears it.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@param value table|nil
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:SetBarber(source, characterId, value)

The table is saved as text and cannot be larger than 262144 bytes. appearance must be a table, could not encode appearance, and appearance is too large use the document name. character not found means this player does not own that id.

fw_characters:updated fires. It does not include the document. Call GetCharacter.

The character menu decides the keys inside appearance and barber. See fw_creator. Worn clothes should go through fw_clothing, which calls SetClothing for you.

local ok, err = exports.fw_characters:SetAppearance(source, characterId, {
    gender = 'Female',
    skintone = 1,
})
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: SaveState
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Saves where they are standing, and their health, for the character this player is playing. It does not change the name or the saved body, clothes, or hair. It does not send the fw_characters:updated message.

--- Saves position and health for the active character.
---@param source integer
---@param state table
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:SaveState(source, state)

Every field is optional, but position is all or nothing. If you send any of x, y, z, or heading, send all four.

Field Rule x, y, z, heading Numbers. Heading is degrees. health Whole number from 0 to 65535. healthCore Whole number from 0 to 100. staminaCore Whole number from 0 to 100. isDead True or false. err When state must be a table state is not a table. player is not loaded That number is not a player in the game. no active character No character is selected. position requires x, y, z, and heading Only part of the position was sent. health must be an integer from 0 to 65535 Health is out of range. healthCore must be an integer from 0 to 100 Health core is out of range. staminaCore must be an integer from 0 to 100 Stamina core is out of range. isDead must be true or false isDead is not a boolean. nothing to save None of these fields were sent. character not found The selected character no longer exists. 
local ok, err = exports.fw_characters:SaveState(source, {
    x = -174.39,
    y = 633.78,
    z = 114.09,
    heading = 90.0,
    health = 540,
    isDead = false,
})
if not ok then
    print(err)
end

The game also reports where the ped is standing. Those reports update the coordinates GetCharacter returns, and they are written to the database on a timer, on disconnect, and when the character is cleared. SaveState writes immediately.

docs.title: DeleteCharacter
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Deletes a character this player owns. Body, clothes, and hair go with it. If it was selected, it is cleared first.

--- Deletes an owned character.
---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
---@return boolean|nil ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_characters:DeleteCharacter(source, characterId)

character not found means this player does not own that id. fw_characters:cleared fires when it was selected. fw_characters:deleted fires after the row is gone.

docs.title: Character record
docs.text:
Field Meaning id Character id. Store this when a row belongs to one character. source Server id the row was loaded for. playerId Account id of the owner. slot Slot on that account, starting at 1. firstName, lastName 1–50 characters. nickname Optional. Nil when empty. gender male or female. birthDate YYYY-MM-DD, or nil. description Lore. Empty string when blank. x, y, z, heading Last known position. A recent sample can be newer than the last database write. health 0–65535. A new character starts at 600. healthCore, staminaCore 0–100. A new character starts at 100. isDead True or false. createdAt When the row was created. lastPlayed When they last played it. Nil until the first selection. hasAppearance, hasClothing, hasBarber True when that document exists. appearance, clothing, barber The documents. Only on GetCharacter and GetActiveCharacter.

GetCharacters leaves the three documents out.

A new character is placed at the default spawn in server/config.lua until something calls SaveState. Birth years must fall between minBirthYear and maxBirthYear in that file. Today that is 1800 through 1899.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
These stay on the server. They are not sent to the player's game. Your script hears one only if it is already running. Put the listener at the top of your script. If your script starts after fw_characters:ready was sent, you missed it. Ask IsReady instead.

The listeners for created, selected, cleared, updated, and deleted run before the call that caused them finishes. The snapshot in the message can be old a moment later. Ask GetCharacter when you need a fresh one.

docs.title: fw_characters:ready
docs.text:
Fires once, when the resource is ready. version is a string such as 1.0.0.

---@param version string
AddEventHandler('fw_characters:ready', function(version)
end)

docs.title: fw_characters:created
docs.text:
The new character is a copy and is not selected yet.

---@param source integer
---@param character table
AddEventHandler('fw_characters:created', function(source, character)
end)

docs.title: fw_characters:selected
docs.text:
A snapshot of the character that just became the one they are playing. Ask GetCharacter when you need a fresh one.

---@param source integer
---@param character table
AddEventHandler('fw_characters:selected', function(source, character)
end)

docs.title: fw_characters:cleared
docs.text:
The player is no longer on that character. It is also sent when they leave, if one was selected. It is not sent when this resource stops.

---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
AddEventHandler('fw_characters:cleared', function(source, characterId)
end)

docs.title: fw_characters:released
docs.text:
Sent to that player's game when the character is cleared, including a switch and a delete. It is not sent when they drop, because their game is already gone. Listen on the client. characterId is the character that just ended. Clear anything you were keeping for that character.

--- The character on this player's game just ended.
---@param characterId integer
---@return nil
RegisterNetEvent('fw_characters:released', function(characterId)
end)

docs.title: fw_characters:relog
docs.text:
Networked. The player's game sends it. /relog does that. The command name is relogCommand in server/config.lua.

The server refuses, and writes a warning, when no character is selected, they are already on the character list, the last switch was too recent (relogCooldownMs), they are in a trade, their ped is dead, or they are hogtied or cuffed. A success saves place, health, and cores, clears the character, writes an info line, and tells that player's game to open the character list.

--- Asks to return to the character list.
---@return nil
TriggerServerEvent('fw_characters:relog')

docs.title: fw_characters:leave
docs.text:
Networked. The player's game sends it. /leave does that. The command name is leaveCommand in server/config.lua.

The same save runs when a character is selected. Then the server drops them with leaveReason, which starts as Left the server. There is no wait between switches for this one. Someone on the character list, with no character selected, is dropped without a save.

--- Asks to save and return to the RedM menu.
---@return nil
TriggerServerEvent('fw_characters:leave')

docs.title: fw_characters:updated
docs.text:
Name or a document was saved. Not fired by SaveState. The new values are not in the event. Call GetCharacter.

---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
AddEventHandler('fw_characters:updated', function(source, characterId)
end)

docs.title: fw_characters:deleted
docs.text:
The character id that was deleted.

---@param source integer
---@param characterId integer
AddEventHandler('fw_characters:deleted', function(source, characterId)
end)

docs.title: A value the player's game can read
docs.text:
Player(source).state.fwCharacterId is the selected character id, or nothing when none is selected. The player's game can read it. The account id is still fwPlayerId from fw_core.

On the server:

local characterId = Player(source).state.fwCharacterId
if characterId == nil then
    return
end

In the player's game:

local characterId = LocalPlayer.state.fwCharacterId

fwHogtied and fwCuffed are true while that ped is hogtied or cuffed. The player's game publishes them about once a second. A switch reads them. They go back to false when the character ends.

docs.title: Where the character is standing
docs.text:
These are networked events: RegisterNetEvent on the server, sent from the player's game with TriggerServerEvent. fw_characters's own client script sends them while the player plays. Another script should save a position with SaveState instead. Do not send these yourself, and do not listen for them. A bad position is ignored.

Message What it does fw_characters:reportPosition The player's game tells the server x, y, z, and heading on a timer. fw_characters:commitPosition The player's game tells the server to store that position now, including when they are leaving.

A jail script can store where they were standing before it moves them:

local character, err = exports.fw_characters:GetActiveCharacter(source)
if character == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

local ok, saveErr = exports.fw_characters:SaveState(source, {
    x = character.x,
    y = character.y,
    z = character.z,
    heading = character.heading,
})
if not ok then
    print(saveErr)
end

docs.title: Server window
docs.text:
These do nothing when a player types them in chat.

Command What it does fw_characters Prints whether the resource is ready, and how many players have a character selected. fw_char_list <serverId> Lists that player's characters. fw_char_create <serverId> <firstName> <lastName> <male\|female> [YYYY-MM-DD] Creates one. Names cannot contain a space here. It does not select the new character. fw_char_select <serverId> <characterId> Selects that character. fw_char_delete <serverId> <characterId> Deletes that character.

serverId is the player number printed by fw_health.

docs.title: fw_clothing
docs.text:
Some calls run on the server. Most run in the player's game. Read the clothes a character is wearing, replace them, or toggle a piece on their body. The saved clothes live on the character. This resource writes them with SetClothing from fw_characters.

The shop still uses the old murphy_clothing and murphy_clothes event names. A new script should use the calls on this page.

Cash lives on fw_money. This shop still does not take any dollars. A later change can call RemoveCash. Job-locked categories stay hidden because there is no job.

fw_creator must keep Config.murphy_clothing true.

docs.title: Clothing document
docs.text:
{
    clothes = {
        hats = { model = 12, texture = 1 },
    },
    outfitId = '1234567', -- '0' when no saved outfit is worn
    outfits = {},
    wearable = {},
}

clothes is what the ped is wearing. Hair and beard stay on the barber document, not here. outfitId is the saved outfit, or '0'.

A write only works while that player is online and has this character selected.

docs.title: IsBandanaEquipped
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes when the worn clothes include a mask (masks) or a large mask (masks_large) with a model number above 0.

--- True when this player is wearing a mask or a large mask.
---@param source integer
---@return boolean
exports.fw_clothing:IsBandanaEquipped(source)

if exports.fw_clothing:IsBandanaEquipped(source) then
    -- hide the face from other players
end

docs.title: GetPlayerClothes
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The worn clothes, turned into the numbers the game uses to draw them. You get an empty result when nothing is saved, or when a clothing slot has no matching picture in the catalog.

--- Worn clothes as asset hashes, keyed by category.
---@param source integer
---@return table clothes
exports.fw_clothing:GetPlayerClothes(source)

Most pieces come back as { hash, tint0, tint1, tint2 }. A piece that is drawn from a story-mode model instead of a regular multiplayer item also carries drawable, albedo, normal, material, and palette, so check for those keys rather than assuming every category has them.

local clothes = exports.fw_clothing:GetPlayerClothes(source)
local hat = clothes.hats
if hat ~= nil then
    print(hat.hash)
end

docs.title: GetPlayerTemperatureProtection
docs.text:
Runs on the server. How many warm pieces and cold pieces are worn, and the protection numbers from the clothing settings.

--- Warm and cold clothing counts for the active character.
---@return table protection
exports.fw_clothing:GetPlayerTemperatureProtection(source)

{
    warmItems = 0,
    coldItems = 0,
    coldProtection = 3,
    heatProtection = 3,
}

local protection = exports.fw_clothing:GetPlayerTemperatureProtection(source)
print(protection.coldProtection)

docs.title: SetClothesForChar
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Saves clothes for the character that is selected right now, then puts them on that player. This is the call a job or uniform script should use.

--- Saves worn clothes for the online player who has this character selected.
--- False and a reason when the character is offline or an entry is not a model and texture.
---@param charid integer|string
---@param clothes table
---@param outfitId integer|string|nil
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_clothing:SetClothesForChar(charid, clothes, outfitId)

charid is fw_characters.id. clothes is { hats = { model = 12, texture = 1 } }. model is the catalog index. texture is a number, or a table { palette, tint0, tint1, tint2 }. Hair and beard are removed from the table before it is saved. Leave outfitId out to store no saved outfit.

err When SetClothesForChar: charid is required The character id is missing. SetClothesForChar: clothes must be a table { category = { model, texture } } clothes is not a table. SetClothesForChar: invalid entry for category '<category>' ... That category has no numeric model. SetClothesForChar: invalid texture for category '<category>' texture is not a number or a table. SetClothesForChar: that character is not selected by an online player Nobody online is playing that character. SetClothesForChar: could not save clothing SetClothing failed. 
local ok, err = exports.fw_clothing:SetClothesForChar(characterId, {
    hats = { model = 12, texture = 1 },
}, nil)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: Calls in the player's game
docs.text:
These run on the player's computer. source is not passed. They look at the clothes already loaded for the character they are playing.

A category is one clothing slot. The names you will use most are hats, shirts_full, vests, boots, neckwear, masks, and gunbelts.

docs.title: AreClothesStillApplied
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Yes when the clothes this resource last put on them are still there. No if clothes were never loaded this visit, or one slot is missing. The check skips bodies_upper and bodies_lower (those are the body, not clothes), and treats neckwear and neckerchiefs as the same slot, since the game stores either name under the other. The character menu uses this after it applies a body, to see if the clothes were wiped off.

--- True when the last clothes this resource applied are still on the ped.
---@return boolean
exports.fw_clothing:AreClothesStillApplied()

if not exports.fw_clothing:AreClothesStillApplied() then
    TriggerEvent('murphy_clothing:loadclothes')
end

docs.title: IsPlayerNaked
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Yes after SetNaked(true) or ToggleNaked has stripped them to the base body. No when their clothes are on.

--- True when this player has been set naked by the clothing script.
---@return boolean
exports.fw_clothing:IsPlayerNaked()

if exports.fw_clothing:IsPlayerNaked() then
    return
end

docs.title: ToggleNaked
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Switches between the base body and the saved clothes. Pass true to also show the small notice. You get back the new naked state.

--- Toggles the base body. Pass true to show the notice.
---@param notify boolean|nil
---@return boolean naked
exports.fw_clothing:ToggleNaked(notify)

A bathhouse script strips them, then puts the clothes back when they leave:

exports.fw_clothing:ToggleNaked(false)

The same action is the message murphy_clothing:toggleNaked. It stays in the player's game.

TriggerEvent('murphy_clothing:toggleNaked', false)

docs.title: SetNaked
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. naked true strips to the base body. naked false puts the saved clothes back. notify true shows the notice.

--- Sets the base body on or off.
---@param naked boolean
---@param notify boolean|nil
---@return boolean naked
exports.fw_clothing:SetNaked(naked, notify)

exports.fw_clothing:SetNaked(true, false)

The same action is murphy_clothing:setNaked in the player's game:

TriggerEvent('murphy_clothing:setNaked', true, false)

murphy_clothing:getNakedState is the old message for the same check as IsPlayerNaked. It does not hand the answer to the script that sent it. Use the call.

docs.title: GetEquippedClothing
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The saved pieces whose model number is above 0. Each one has model, texture, and category.

--- Worn categories from the saved clothes on this computer.
---@return table equipped
exports.fw_clothing:GetEquippedClothing()

local equipped = exports.fw_clothing:GetEquippedClothing()
if equipped.hats ~= nil then
    print(equipped.hats.model)
end

--- Equipped categories, with model and texture.

print(categories.boots and categories.boots.model)

docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Yes when that category has a saved model above 0. This stays yes while the player has temporarily taken the piece off with a toggle.

---@return boolean

docs.text:

docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The same kind of result as the server call, plus categories, the list of worn category names. A cold-weather script on the player's computer can read it without asking the server.

docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Ask about a list of categories. For each one you get owned (the outfit includes it) and on (it is showing right now). fw_weapons uses this to see the gunbelt.

--- owned and on, for each category name you pass.
---@param categories string[]
---@return table states
exports.fw_clothing:GetClothingToggleState(categories)

local states = exports.fw_clothing:GetClothingToggleState({ 'gunbelts' })
local belt = states.gunbelts

docs.title: ToggleClothingCategory
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Takes that saved piece off, or puts it back on. Works for any category the outfit owns, not only the ones listed under ToggleClothingComponent below. You get yes when it is on afterwards. You get no when the outfit has no such piece.

--- Toggles one saved category. False when the outfit has none.
---@param category string
---@return boolean on
exports.fw_clothing:ToggleClothingCategory(category)

local on = exports.fw_clothing:ToggleClothingCategory('hats')

The message murphy_clothes:Equip-UnequipCategory does the same toggle. It stays in the player's game.

TriggerEvent('murphy_clothes:Equip-UnequipCategory', 'hats')

docs.title: ToggleClothingComponent
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The wheel uses this to take a piece off or put it back, with a short matching animation (reaching for the hat, adjusting the belt, and so on). Only a fixed list of categories can be toggled this way: hats, masks, eyewear, headwear, hat_accessories, neckwear, neckerchiefs, neckties, shirts_full, vests, suspenders, coats, coats_closed, coats_heavy, cloaks, ponchos, capes, gloves, gauntlets, gunbelts, gunbelt_accs, pants, chaps, spats, boots, boot_accessories, accessories, satchels, badges, and aprons. Anything outside that list, or a category name that is not a string, is refused. You also get no while another toggle's animation is still playing, or while the player is dead. Otherwise you get yes — the toggle has started, even if that slot turns out to already be empty.

--- Toggles the piece in this category on the player's body.
---@param category string
---@return boolean ok
exports.fw_clothing:ToggleClothingComponent(category)

exports.fw_clothing:ToggleClothingComponent('gloves')

The message murphy_clothing:toggleComponent is the same call. The command /toggleclothing hats is the same call from chat.

TriggerEvent('murphy_clothing:toggleComponent', 'hats')

docs.title: GetWornClothingCategories
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The category names from the list above that the player's outfit actually owns — the ones ToggleClothingComponent can act on. A piece they hid with a toggle is still in the list, because the outfit still owns it.

--- Category names the player can take off and put back on.
---@return string[] categories
exports.fw_clothing:GetWornClothingCategories()

local categories = exports.fw_clothing:GetWornClothingCategories()
for index = 1, #categories do
    print(categories[index])
end

slots is a map. The key is a name you choose, such as shirt. The value is a list of category names to look at. You get back only the slots that have an action. A slot can include collar, bandana, tuck, or variation.

docs.text:

clothesData is { hats = { model = 1, texture = 0 } }. tint0, tint1, and tint2 are optional. Leave ped out to use the player's character. You get no when clothesData is not a table. A category or model that does not exist in the catalog is skipped quietly — ok only reports whether clothesData itself was a table, not whether every piece in it was understood, so check the result with GetEquippedCategories afterwards if you need to be sure something was actually applied.

--- Puts several pieces on a character in this player's game.
---@param clothesData table
---@param ped integer|nil
---@return boolean ok
exports.fw_clothing:EquipMultipleClothes(clothesData, ped)

A costume script on the player's computer:

exports.fw_clothing:EquipMultipleClothes({
    hats = { model = 1, texture = 0 },
    shirts_full = { model = 5, texture = 2 },
})

The message murphy_clothes:EquipMultipleClothes is the same call.

TriggerEvent('murphy_clothes:EquipMultipleClothes', {
    hats = { model = 1, texture = 0 },
})

docs.text:

--- True when a mask is in the saved clothes on this computer.

end

docs.title: Messages
docs.text: A message on the server is heard with AddEventHandler. A message in the player's game is heard with AddEventHandler when it stays there, or RegisterNetEvent when the server can send it. Your script hears one only if it is already running. Put the listener at the top of your script.

docs.title: murphy_clothing:clothesUpdated
docs.text:
Stays on the server. Sent after clothes are saved, from the shop or from SetClothesForChar. A uniform script can wait for this, then read the clothes back:

---@param source integer
---@param charid integer
---@param clothes table
AddEventHandler('murphy_clothing:clothesUpdated', function(source, charid, clothes)
    print(charid)
end)

docs.title: murphy_clothing:loadclothes
docs.text:
Sent from the server to the player's game. Their game puts the saved clothes back on. The character menu sends the local version of this after a body is applied. You can send it yourself after you know the clothes were wiped off:

TriggerEvent('murphy_clothing:loadclothes')

docs.title: murphy_clothes:OnClothingChanged
docs.text:
Stays in the player's game. Sent when a category is taken off or put on. category is the slot name. equipped is yes when it is on. fw_weapons listens so a missing gunbelt puts the guns away.

---@param category string
---@param equipped boolean
AddEventHandler('murphy_clothes:OnClothingChanged', function(category, equipped)
    if category == 'gunbelts' and not equipped then
        print('belt off')
    end
end)

docs.text:
Stays in the player's game. Sent after the sleeve or collar changes. It has no extra information. Read IsSleeveRolled if you need the new state.

AddEventHandler('fw_clothing:sleeveChanged', function()
end)

Message What it does What to do murphy_clothes:CheckBandana Looks at the mask, then sends murphy_clothes:BandanaStatus. Prefer IsBandanaEquipped. murphy_clothes:BandanaStatus true when a mask is on.     print(protection.coldProtection)

An optional keybind does the same thing if the server sets Config.ClothesManagement.GetNakedKeybind. /toggleclothing <category> The player Same toggle as ToggleClothingComponent. /ClothesManagement A player who has fw.admin (see fw_admin) Opens the wearable/body management menu. docs.title: fw_core
docs.text:
Runs on the server. This is the account for a player who has joined. Your script reads that account here.

The player's game only prints a log line. Reading an account stays on the server.

docs.title: Why you check in
docs.text:
fw_core has a version written as three numbers, such as 1.1.0.

Your script only cares about the first number. Right now that number is 1. It means "these are the calls on this page." The other two numbers can go up when something is added that an old script can ignore. You never pass those two numbers.

RegisterResource(1) is a check-in. You are saying "I was written while the first number was 1." You do not pass your script's name. The server already knows who called.

The check-in does two jobs:

  • While this server is still on 1, the call succeeds. Typing fw_health in the server window lists your script.
  • If a later update changes the calls so a script written for 1 would break, the first number becomes 2. Your script then gets a clear line in the server window, telling you to update it, instead of failing in the middle of someone's visit.

The other calls on this page still work if you skip the check-in. Do it anyway, once, after IsReady says yes. The example on the first page already does this. Copy that.

GetVersion and GetApiVersion are for looking. A normal script does not call them.

docs.title: IsReady
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Ask this before you use anything else on this page.

It stays no until two things are done. fw_core has a normal version, such as 1.1.0, and the player list has been created in the database. If the version is wrong, or the player list cannot be created, the server window shows an error. IsReady stays no. People trying to join are turned away.

The server can say fw_core has started a moment before this is true. Checking once is too early. Keep checking for about two minutes. The example on the first page does that.

--- True when other scripts can use fw_core.
---@return boolean ready
exports.fw_core:IsReady()

if not exports.fw_core:IsReady() then
    return
end

docs.title: GetVersion
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Gives the full version, such as 1.1.0. A normal script does not need this. It does not check the database. It can give you a version while IsReady is still no.

--- The version, such as '1.1.0', or nothing if the version is not three numbers.
---@return string|nil version
exports.fw_core:GetVersion()

print(exports.fw_core:GetVersion())

docs.title: GetApiVersion
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Gives the first number of the version, such as 1. A normal script does not need this. RegisterResource already compares that number for you.

--- The first number of the version, or nothing if the version is not three numbers.
---@return integer|nil apiVersion
exports.fw_core:GetApiVersion()

print(exports.fw_core:GetApiVersion())

docs.title: RegisterResource
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Check in, as described in Why you check in. Call it once, from your own script, after IsReady says yes.

--- Checks this script in for a set of calls.
--- False when fw_core is not ready, the call did not come from another script, or the number does not match.
---@param requiredApiVersion integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_core:RegisterResource(requiredApiVersion)

Pass 1. That is the first number of the version. 1.0 also works. 1.5, 0, and words do not. Pass the number this server is on. Passing 2 while the server is on 1 fails, and the reason names both numbers.

In the lines below, your-script stands in for your script's folder name.

What you get back When fw_core is not ready The player list is not ready yet. Keep checking, as on the first page. RegisterResource must be called from another resource The call came from fw_core itself. Put it in your own script. your-script: required API version must be a positive integer You did not pass a whole number above 0. Pass 1. fw_core API 1 is incompatible with required API 2; your-script needs a newer core You asked for 2, and this server is still on 1. fw_core API 2 is incompatible with required API 1; update your-script for API 2 A later server is on 2, and your script still passes 1. Update the script, then pass 2.

The same line is written in the server window log. If it fails, stop there and read the line. The example below does that.

local Logger = Import('logger').Logger
local ok, err = exports.fw_core:RegisterResource(1)
if not ok then
    Logger:Error(err, { prefix = 'your-script' })
    return
end

Calling it again from the same script replaces the stored number. Stopping your script removes the check-in. There is no separate call to undo it.

docs.title: GetPlayer
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Gives a snapshot of the account for a player who has finished joining. You get nothing while they are still connecting, and nothing if that player number is not in the game. Changing the snapshot does not save.

--- The connected account, or nothing when that player has not finished joining.
---@param source integer
---@return table|nil player
exports.fw_core:GetPlayer(source)

source is the player's number for this visit. The fields are in Account.

local player = exports.fw_core:GetPlayer(source)
if player == nil then
    return
end
print(('source %d is account %d'):format(source, player.id))

docs.title: GetPlayerById
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The same account, found by account id instead of player number. You get nothing when that person is offline. This does not look in the database for someone who is not in the game.

--- The connected account for an account id, or nothing when that person is offline.
---@param playerId integer
---@return table|nil player
exports.fw_core:GetPlayerById(playerId)

playerId is the account id, fw_players.id.

local player = exports.fw_core:GetPlayerById(1)
if player == nil then
    return
end

docs.title: GetSourceByPlayerId
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The player number for an account that is online. You get nothing when that person is offline. Use this when you saved an account id and need to send that person a message in their game.

--- The player number for an online account, or nothing when that person is offline.
---@param playerId integer
---@return integer|nil source
exports.fw_core:GetSourceByPlayerId(playerId)

local target = exports.fw_core:GetSourceByPlayerId(playerId)
if target == nil then
    return
end
TriggerClientEvent('my_resource:notify', target)

docs.title: SetBan
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Saves a ban on a license, or lifts one. This writes the player list. It does not remove anyone from the server. If they are online, drop them yourself after a ban you want to start now. If you do not, the ban starts the next time they try to join.

license is their Rockstar license, including license: at the front. You can read it from GetPlayer while they are online, or from fw_admin in the server window. A license longer than 64 characters is refused with the same reason as a license that does not start with license:. That is the size of the license column.

untilTime is a whole number of seconds since 1970, the usual unix time. 0 is a ban that does not expire. Pass nothing (nil) to lift the ban. A time that is already past is refused.

You get false and a reason when the player list is not ready, the license is missing or not in the list, or the time is not 0 or a future time. Nothing is written in those cases.

--- Saves a ban, or lifts one when untilTime is nothing.
--- False and a reason when the license or the time is refused, or the save fails.
---@param license string
---@param untilTime integer|nil 0 does not expire, nil lifts the ban
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_core:SetBan(license, untilTime)

local Logger = Import('logger').Logger
local player = exports.fw_core:GetPlayer(source)
if player == nil then
    return
end

local ok, err = exports.fw_core:SetBan(player.license, 0)
if not ok then
    Logger:Warn(err, { prefix = 'your-script' })
    return
end

DropPlayer(source, 'You are banned from this server.')

A ban of one day is os.time() + (24 * 3600). Lift it with SetBan(license, nil).

docs.title: Account
docs.text:
GetPlayer, GetPlayerById, fw_core:playerLoaded, and fw_core:playerDropped all give you this. It is a snapshot. Changing it does not save.

Field Meaning id Account id. Save this when something belongs to the person, not to one character. source Player number for this visit. It changes when they join again. license Their Rockstar license, including license: at the front. steam Steam id, or nothing. discord Discord id, or nothing. name The name they joined with. role A label on the account. A new account uses account.defaultRole in the config, which starts as user. This does not make them an admin. Use fw_admin. characterSlots How many characters this account may create. A new account uses account.defaultCharacterSlots, which starts at 5. An account that already has a number keeps it. warnings A stored count. Nothing happens because of it. banned Always false here. A banned license never finishes joining. bannedUntil Always 0 here.

There is no call to change role, warnings, or character slots. SetBan changes a ban. Role and warnings are read again the next time that person joins. A ban is read again the next time they try to join. The character slot count is read again the next time a character is created.

A person is turned away while joining when the database is down, the server is still starting, RedM did not send a license, the license is banned, or that same license is already in the server.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text: These stay on the server. They are not sent to the player's game. Your script hears one only if it is already running. Put the listener at the top of your script. If your script starts later, you missed the message. Ask the matching call instead, where one is listed.

docs.title: fw_core:ready
docs.text:
Sent once, when the player list is ready. A script that starts later missed it. Ask IsReady.

--- The player list is ready. version is text such as '1.1.0'. apiVersion is the first number, such as 1.
---@param version string
---@param apiVersion integer
---@return nil
AddEventHandler('fw_core:ready', function(version, apiVersion)
end)

docs.title: fw_core:playerLoaded
docs.text:
Sent when a player has finished joining. player is a snapshot of the account. Ask GetPlayer again when you need a fresh one.

--- player is a snapshot of the account. Ask GetPlayer again when you need a fresh one.
---@param source integer player's number for this visit
---@param player table
---@return nil
AddEventHandler('fw_core:playerLoaded', function(source, player)
    print(player.id)
end)

docs.title: fw_core:playerDropped
docs.text:
Sent when that player leaves. player is a snapshot taken before the account is forgotten.

--- player is a snapshot taken before the account is forgotten.
---@param source integer player's number for this visit
---@param player table
---@return nil
AddEventHandler('fw_core:playerDropped', function(source, player)
end)

docs.title: A value the player's game can read
docs.text:
Player(source).state.fwPlayerId is the account id. This is the only state bag on this resource. In the player's game:

local playerId = LocalPlayer.state.fwPlayerId
if playerId == nil then
    return
end

On the server, the same value is player.id from GetPlayer. Prefer that call when you are already on the server. The state bag is there so the player's game can see the account id without asking.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
The settings are in resources/[framework]/fw_core/shared/config.lua, on FwCoreConfig. Change a value, then restart fw_core. Another script does not set these, and there is no export for them.

map.reveal shows every region when it is true. Places the character has never visited are drawn. false leaves fog over those places.

map.revealAgainMs is how long to wait, in milliseconds, after the character is chosen before the fog is set again. The character menu puts the fog back, so this runs a second time. It starts at 4000.

account.defaultCharacterSlots is how many characters a new account may create. It starts at 5. An account that already has a number in the database keeps that number.

account.defaultRole is the label stored on a new account. It starts at user. It does not grant staff. Staff is fw_admin.

ban.permanent is the sentence for a ban that does not expire. ban.until is the sentence for a ban that ends, and %s in that sentence is the time. ban.dateFormat is the pattern for that time. The clock is UTC. The pattern starts at %Y-%m-%d %H:%M.

join holds the sentences a person sees while connecting.

  • checking is the line shown while the account is read.
  • starting is shown when the player list is still coming up.
  • database is shown when the database cannot be used.
  • noLicense is shown when RedM did not send a Rockstar license.
  • alreadyHere is shown when that same license is already in the server.
  • failed is shown when the account could not be loaded.
  • unknownName is stored when the name they joined with is empty.

A blank join or ban sentence warns once in the server window, and the player sees that the message could not be read. A bad time pattern puts the unix time in the ban sentence. A bad slot count stays at 5, a bad role stays at user, and a bad map delay stays at 4000. Debug lines stay on the fw_core_debug convar. Set that in the server window. It does not live in this file.

docs.title: Server window
docs.text:
Type fw_health in the server window. It writes INFO lines for whether fw_core is ready, the version, how many players are connected, and which scripts registered. Nothing happens if a player types it in chat.

A line about one player is also written to that player's console, the F8 window. A refusal is a warning. A failure is an error. A result, such as an account connecting, is info. Debug lines stay off until you set fw_core_debug to true.

docs.title: fw_core:log
docs.text:
Sent to one player's game. It copies one server line into that player's console. You do not send this, and you do not need to listen for it.

--- Copies one server line into this player's console.
---@param message string
---@param level string error, warn, or info
---@return nil
RegisterNetEvent('fw_core:log', function(message, level)
end)

docs.title: fw_creator
docs.text:
