The character menu. Players use it to make a character and to play one. Create and read characters with fw_characters — that is the page to build on. This page exists for two reasons: to show where the menu stores things on the character, and to document the handful of calls and messages this menu genuinely exposes for another script to use (pausing appearance updates while a player is shapeshifted, sharing a face with nearby players, and a couple of admin commands).

Config.framework in shared/config.lua must stay fw. Anything else and character select never answers.

The number of characters an account can create is characterSlots on the account, not Config.Slots in this menu. The menu sends Config.Slots to the player's game only as a fallback, for the moment before the server has answered.

docs.title: Where the menu saves things
docs.text:
What the player enters Where it goes Name firstName and lastName Gender male or female Birthday birthDate as YYYY-MM-DD Lore description Chosen spawn SaveState, right after a new character is created Body and face appearance Hair and makeup barber Clothes fw_clothing, not this menu

Config.murphy_clothing must stay true while fw_clothing is running.

docs.title: Body document
docs.text:
SetAppearance stores the table the menu already built. These are the keys other code reads:

Key Meaning gender Male or Female. skintone Skin tone index. pedmodel.model Model name, such as mp_male. pedmodel.outfit Outfit preset on that model. head, upperbody, lowerbody, body, waist Body indexes. teeth, eyes Face component indexes. height A scale, 1.0 is the model default. expressions The face sliders. Keyed by slider name. See GetCachedExpressions.

Replace the document by sending the whole table. Do not write one key by itself and expect the rest to remain unless you read the current document first and send it back with your change.

docs.title: Hair document
docs.text:
{
    hairstyle = {},
    overlays = {},
    permanentoverlay = {},
    outfitId = '1230456',
    presets = {
        {
            hairstyle = {},
            overlays = {},
            name = 'Base',
            outfitId = '1230456',
            price = 0,
            gender = 'male',
        },
    },
}

The first save during character creation uses the preset name Base.

docs.title: Health sent to the menu
docs.text:
When a character is selected, the client receives:

{
    hOuter = 600, -- character.health
    hInner = 100, -- character.healthCore
    sOuter = 100, -- always 100; there is no second stamina field
    sInner = 100, -- character.staminaCore
}

That message is murphy_creator:HealthFromCore. The server sends it to the player's game. This menu does not save health when the player leaves. Use SaveState on fw_characters for that.

docs.title: Messages the menu uses
docs.text:
These keep the old murphy_creator names so the screen did not have to be renamed. A new script should listen to the messages on fw_characters instead of most of these.

A networked message only reaches a listener that is already running when the message is sent. If your script starts later, you missed it; use the matching call instead, where one is listed.

Event Direction What it does murphy_creator:getCharacters Networked, player's game to server Asks for the character list. murphy_creator:LaunchCharSelect Networked, server to player's game Opens the list. murphy_creator:CharSelectFailed Networked, server to player's game A reason string. The client writes it to the log and tries once more. fw_creator:selectCharacter Networked, player's game to server Selects that character id, then sends health. murphy_creator:deleteCharacter Networked, player's game to server The argument is the index in the list last sent to this player, not a character id. murphy_creator:HealthFromCore Networked, server to player's game The health table above.

fw_characters:selected is the event to use when your resource needs to know a character was chosen. A spawn script listens there, not on fw_creator:selectCharacter:

AddEventHandler('fw_characters:selected', function(source, character)
    print(character.id)
end)

murphy_creator:HealthFromCore is the health table above, sent by the server to the player's game. It is networked — your script only hears it if it is already running when the server sends it. Listen only if you are drawing your own health bar from that menu:

RegisterNetEvent('murphy_creator:HealthFromCore', function(health)
    print(health.hOuter)
end)

The menu also uses these messages. A new script should keep using fw_characters. They are listed so an older script can be matched to a name.

Message Direction What it does murphy_creator:GetHealthValues Networked, player's game to server Asks for the health table. The answer is murphy_creator:HealthFromCore. murphy_creator:OpenCharSelect Local, either way Opens the character list again. fw_creator:openSelect Networked, server to that player's game Opens the character list after a switch. The server is the sender. murphy_creator:LaunchCreator Local, player's game Opens the body editor for a new character. murphy_creator:deleteCharacterClient Networked, server to player's game The list index that was just deleted. murphy_creator:SecondChance Networked, server to player's game Opens the body editor again. /secondchance sends this. fw_creator:characterSelected Networked, player's game The menu's own note that a character was picked. Then it loads the body. Prefer fw_characters:selected. murphy_creator:loadskin Networked, player's game Puts the saved body back on. The reload command sends this. murphy_creator:loadskinvorp Networked, player's game The same reload, used after the model is already the right one. murphy_creator:localExpressionsReady Networked, player's game The face sliders and eyes/teeth are ready to share. The menu publishes them. murphy_creator:client:skinApplied Local, player's game The body finished applying. See below. murphy_creator:client:characterCreated Local, player's game The new character was just saved by the menu. No arguments. murphy_creator:applystarteroutfit Networked, server to player's game Dresses the character in the configured starter outfit again. See below. murphy_barber_creator:loadbarberoverlay Networked, player's game Puts the saved hair and makeup back on. murphy_barber_creator:loadbarberoverlayOnCharacter Networked, player's game Same, for a character id you pass. murphy_barber_creator:updatehairstyle Networked, player's game to server The barber saves hair. A new script uses SetBarber on fw_characters. murphy_barber_creator:clotheitem Networked, player's game The barber applies the saved hair and makeup to a ped. murphy_creator:triggerCallback Networked, server to player's game The menu's private question. A new script does not send this. murphy_creator:responseCallback Networked, player's game to server The answer to that question. A new script does not send this.

docs.title: A hook for your own clothing script
docs.text:
murphy_creator:client:skinApplied is a local event, fired on the player's own game right after the menu finishes putting a saved body back on. It exists so a clothing script that is not fw_clothing can know the body just got rebuilt (the rebuild strips worn clothes) and re-dress the player without waiting for them to type a reload command.

--- ped is the entity handle for the player's own character in this game.
---@param ped integer
AddEventHandler('murphy_creator:client:skinApplied', function(ped)
    exports.fw_creator:ReassertLocalExpressions()
end)

If your clothing script's own reload event is listed in Config.ExternalClothingEvents in shared/config.lua, the menu fires that event too at the same moment, and you do not need to add a listener for murphy_creator:client:skinApplied at all.

docs.title: Applying the starter outfit again
docs.text:
murphy_creator:applystarteroutfit is networked, server to player's game. A server script can send it to a player to make the menu dress their character in the configured starter outfit again — the same clothes a brand-new character spawns in before they own anything of their own.

TriggerClientEvent('murphy_creator:applystarteroutfit', source)

This only does something while Config.CreatorClothing.starterOutfit.enabled is true in shared/config.lua. With it off, or with no preset configured for that character's gender, the player's game quietly does nothing.

docs.title: Calls in the player's game
docs.text: Create and read characters with fw_characters. These calls are for a script that changes the body the player is looking at, such as an animal form, or that needs to keep a shared face in sync.

docs.title: SetAppearancePaused
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Pass true before you change them into something that is not their character, such as a wolf. The character menu stops painting the human face on top. Pass false when they are themselves again.

This also sets LocalPlayer.state.murphy_appearance_paused. Only this player's game can read that value.

--- Pauses face and clothes updates on this player's game.
---@param paused boolean
exports.fw_creator:SetAppearancePaused(paused)

exports.fw_creator:SetAppearancePaused(true)

docs.title: IsAppearancePaused
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Yes while that pause is on.

--- True while appearance updates are paused on this computer.
---@return boolean
exports.fw_creator:IsAppearancePaused()

if exports.fw_creator:IsAppearancePaused() then
    return
end

docs.title: IsPedModelCharacter
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Yes when the loaded character is a custom model, not mp_male or mp_female. A barber script uses this so it does not paint skin and makeup onto a copied face.

--- True when this character is not mp_male or mp_female.
---@return boolean
exports.fw_creator:IsPedModelCharacter()

if exports.fw_creator:IsPedModelCharacter() then
    return
end

docs.title: GetCachedExpressions
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The face sliders, or nothing when none are loaded. The keys are the expression names the game uses. Changing the table does not change the face. Call ReassertLocalExpressions after you want them drawn again.

--- The face sliders, or nothing when none are loaded.
---@return table|nil expressions
exports.fw_creator:GetCachedExpressions()

local expressions = exports.fw_creator:GetCachedExpressions()
if expressions == nil then
    return
end

docs.title: PublishLocalExpressions
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Copies the current face sliders into the murphy_expressions state bag so other players' games can draw the same face on this player. The menu already does this on its own, about every two seconds. Call it yourself only if your script changed the sliders and cannot wait for that next tick.

--- Shares the local face sliders with other players.
exports.fw_creator:PublishLocalExpressions()

exports.fw_creator:PublishLocalExpressions()

docs.title: ClearLocalExpressions
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Clears murphy_expressions. Call it when this player leaves the character, so the next person nearby does not keep the old face.

--- Clears the shared face sliders.
exports.fw_creator:ClearLocalExpressions()

exports.fw_creator:ClearLocalExpressions()

docs.title: PublishLocalFaceComps
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Shares the eyes and teeth so a player who walks up later still sees them. The menu already does this alongside PublishLocalExpressions.

--- Shares eyes and teeth with other players.
exports.fw_creator:PublishLocalFaceComps()

exports.fw_creator:PublishLocalFaceComps()

docs.title: ReassertLocalExpressions
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Draws the saved face sliders on the local character again. Call it right after your script rebuilds that character, such as in the hook in A hook for your own clothing script. You get no while appearance is paused, while there are no sliders, or while the character is missing or dead.

--- Draws the saved face sliders again. False when there is nothing to draw.
---@return boolean ok
exports.fw_creator:ReassertLocalExpressions()

exports.fw_creator:ReassertLocalExpressions()

docs.title: GetMurphyAssets
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The full clothing and barber picture catalog this menu knows about — every hair, makeup and clothing option, grouped by gender and category. A normal script does not need it. Read worn clothes with fw_clothing.

--- The clothing and barber picture list.
---@return table assets
exports.fw_creator:GetMurphyAssets()

local assets = exports.fw_creator:GetMurphyAssets()

docs.title: State bags
docs.text:
Name Who can read it What it is murphy_appearance_paused This player's game only Yes while SetAppearancePaused(true) is on. PlayerIsInCharacterShops The server and every player's game Yes while this player is in the character menu. No after they pick a character. murphy_expressions The server and every player's game The face sliders. Written by PublishLocalExpressions. murphy_face_comps The server and every player's game Eyes and teeth. Written by PublishLocalFaceComps. murphyLocale Everyone, on the global state A language name, if another resource sets GlobalState.murphyLocale. This menu reads it. It does not set it.

A script that should not teleport someone who is still picking a character:

if Player(source).state.PlayerIsInCharacterShops then
    return
end

On the player's own game:

if LocalPlayer.state.murphy_appearance_paused then
    return
end

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
There are two separate places that decide who may delete a character: one for the menu's own delete button, one for the /deletechar admin command. They are not the same setting.

Command Who What it does /mc The player Reloads their body on the client. The name comes from Config.LoadSkinCommand in shared/config.lua; a server can rename it. /deletechar [characterId] Someone fw_admin says is an admin, or a role or identifier listed under Config.Commands.deleteCharacter Deletes the caller's own character by id. The server console passes the permission check but the command still refuses to run for it, because the delete needs the owning player's account. Someone else's character id fails with an error from fw_characters. /secondchance [serverId] The same kind of check, under Config.Commands.secondChance. The console may run this one. Opens the body menu again for that player.

The delete button inside the menu itself (murphy_creator:deleteCharacter above) is governed separately, by Config.CharacterDeletion in shared/config.lua. When Config.CharacterDeletion.restrictToRoles is false, every player may delete their own character from the menu, regardless of the /deletechar command's role list. Set Config.CharacterDeletion.enabled to false to turn that button off entirely.

docs.title: fw_guide
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. This is the help screen. Type /guide to open it. Type /guide again, or press Escape, to close it.

The first subject is the large card on the left. The next ones fill the cards on the right. The line along the bottom describes the card you are on. Enter opens that subject. Escape steps back. On the front page, Escape closes help.

A subject opens as one of two screens.

A reading page is the Player screen. The title at the top is the card you opened. The writing is in up to three columns. Up and down scroll it. The corner says SCROLL and BACK.

A card row is the Roles screen. The pictures sit in a line, with a title and a short line under each one. Left and right move the red frame. Enter opens that card's reading page. Activities uses this screen.

Both are filled in from client/pages.lua. The first entry is the large card. screen = 'article' is the reading page. screen = 'row' is the card row.

A column is a list of blocks. A block is one of these:

  • heading — the small capital line, such as Satchel.
  • body — the paragraph under it.
  • rule — a thin line between two paragraphs.
  • icons — a row of circles. The names that draw are heart, bolt, cross, bag, and swap.
  • image — a worn picture. art is the file name in html/art, without .svg. caption is the line under it.

A row card uses title, blurb, and art. Give it columns when Enter should open a reading page.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text: Both run in the player's game.

docs.title: Open
docs.text:
--- Shows the help screen.
---@return nil
exports.fw_guide:Open()

exports.fw_guide:Open()

docs.title: Close
docs.text:
--- Hides the help screen.
---@return nil
exports.fw_guide:Close()

exports.fw_guide:Close()

/guide is a client command. It takes no arguments. A script should call Open or Close instead of running the command for the player.

docs.title: fw_inventory
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Give a player an item, take one away, add a new kind of item, or open a second grid such as a chest or a pouch.

fw_satchel is the screen the player sees. It draws their bag and, when one is open, the chest or pouch beside it. Your script does not open that screen itself, except with OpenStorage, which opens both.

Ask IsReady first. If you also listen for fw_inventory:ready and your script starts later, you missed that message. Ask IsReady instead.

A second grid is the same kind of squares as the player's bag. There are two ways to open one. A chest, a safety deposit box, a wagon, or a horse bag is a storage your script registers, then opens. A pouch is an item the player uses. Those are different jobs. Both are below.

docs.title: A chest, a wagon, or a horse
docs.text:
Register the storage when your script starts. The items stay in the database. The registration itself is remembered only while your script is running. When your script stops, the spot in the world goes away, and a restart does not leave a second prompt.

source is the player's number for this visit.

exports.fw_inventory:RegisterStorage({
    id = 'chest:valentine_1',
    label = 'Chest',
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    categories = { 'materials', 'tools' },
    acceptWeapons = false,
    adminOnly = false,
    shared = true,
    characters = nil,
    locations = {
        { coords = vector3(-308.0, 776.0, 118.0), distance = 2.0 },
    },
})

Hold at that spot opens the chest. A horse bag or a wagon has no locations. Your horse or wagon script calls OpenRegistered when the player is there.

  • id is how the chest is remembered. chest:valentine_1 is one chest. chest:valentine_2 is a different chest. Use lowercase letters, digits, underscore, colon, and hyphen. Start with a letter or a digit. No spaces. Keep it to 64 characters or fewer. Do not start it with item:. That prefix is the storage inside a pouch.
  • shared = true is one set of items for everyone, saved under that id. A town chest.
  • shared = false is one set of items per character, saved as that id plus :character: plus the character's id. A safety deposit box, a horse bag, or a wagon. Register it once. Each character gets their own contents the first time they open it. The finished name still has to fit in 64 characters.
  • characters, on a shared storage, is the list of character ids allowed to open it. Leave it out, or pass nothing, and any character can open it. A personal storage ignores this list. The character id comes from fw_characters.
  • adminOnly = true means only a player fw_admin counts as an admin can open it. Anyone else gets You cannot open that. It still follows shared. A shared admin chest is one grid. A personal admin chest is one grid per admin. Leave it out and it is false.
  • locations is optional. Each entry is coords and distance. With no locations, nothing is placed in the world.
  • contents is optional. A list of { name = 'bread', count = 2 }. The first time that storage is opened, and it has no saved row yet, those piles are packed in. A later open shows what was left. Taking them out does not pack them again. An empty chest stays empty. A shared chest packs once for everyone. A personal chest (shared = false) packs once for each character, because each character has a different saved grid. Dollars in that list stay on the chest until someone takes them out. A bad list comes back from RegisterStorage as the reason. Leave contents out and the chest starts empty.
  • width and height are how many squares, from 1 to 24. The example is 8 across and 6 down.
  • label is the title the player sees, and the words on the prompt. Leave it out and the title is Storage.
  • The bag opens at the same time, with the chest beside it. The player drags items between them.
  • The player must already be playing a character. Otherwise you get Select a character first.

A script that registered a storage opens it with OpenRegistered, so the personal name, the character list, and adminOnly are applied. OpenStorage is the low-level open. Use it for a storage you did not register. A direct OpenStorage does not add :character:, does not check the character list, and does not check adminOnly.

One person can have a chest open at a time. The next person gets Someone is using that. One player can have one of these open. Opening a second one closes the first.

CloseStorage hides the chest and leaves the bag open. Closing the bag on the player's screen also closes the chest — that happens on the player's screen, not on this page.

To make a chest larger later, register it again with the same name and a bigger width or height, or call OpenStorage with that same name. The items stay. Making it smaller, while an item sits on a square that would disappear, comes back as Make room in there first. Nothing is moved.

docs.title: Which items can go in
docs.text:
Every item has a category. The categories are ammo, animals, documents, food, herbs, horse, medical, tools, valuables, currency, weapons, materials, and container. A pouch uses container. Dollars use currency. The balance a shop spends is on fw_money.

  • Leave categories out, and every category is allowed, except weapons when acceptWeapons is false.
  • Pass a list, and only those categories can be dragged in. Herbs and tools: categories = { 'herbs', 'tools' }.
  • An empty list, categories = {}, takes nothing.
  • A name that is not in the list above comes back as unknown category.
  • Something other than a list of strings, such as a number or a single string, comes back as Invalid storage categories.
  • acceptWeapons is its own yes or no. It is not worked out from the category list. Leave it out on RegisterStorage and it is false, so a gun stays out. true lets weapons in. A weapon is an item whose category is weapons, or one that has a kit or a weapon hash. This is checked when the item is dragged in, including when that open came from a registration. A direct OpenStorage that was never registered still accepts weapons, so an older caller keeps working. A registered storage that refuses a gun shows Weapons do not go in there.

When the player drags the wrong kind of item, they see That does not go in there. The bag itself takes every category.

A pouch, or any other item that has a container block, cannot be put into a chest, a wagon, a horse bag, or another pouch. The player sees A container cannot go in there. Taking that pouch back out into the bag is allowed. Handing one to another player is allowed.

exports.fw_inventory:OpenRegistered(source, 'chest:valentine_1')

docs.title: A pouch, or any item that holds other items
docs.text:
A pouch is an item in the bag. When the player uses it, a second grid opens, the same kind of grid as a chest. You do not call OpenStorage for a pouch. The item does that.

You add the pouch the same way you add any other item: a file in items/, or RegisterItem. The extra part is container.

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RegisterItem({
    name = 'seed_pouch',
    label = 'Seed Pouch',
    category = 'container',
    width = 2,
    height = 2,
    stack = 1,
    description = 'A small pouch for seeds.',
    container = {
        label = 'Seed pouch',
        width = 4,
        height = 4,
        categories = { 'herbs' },
    },
})
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

The same fields work in an item file. The name is the key, so you leave name out of the file. The item file section shows that shape.

items/container.lua already ships with a pouch named herb_pouch, 2 by 2 in the bag with a 6-by-10 grid inside that only takes herbs. You can give that one to a player without registering anything, the same way you'd give any other item that ships in that folder.

What you pass:

  • category on the pouch itself is container. That is the filter on the left of the bag. The list inside container.categories is what the pouch accepts.
  • width and height on the item are how many squares the pouch takes in the bag. Here that is 2 by 2.
  • container.width and container.height are how many squares are inside the pouch, from 1 to 24. Here that is 4 by 4.
  • container.label is the title of that second grid.
  • container.categories follows the same rules as a chest. Leave it out and the pouch takes anything. { 'herbs' } takes herbs only. A pouch still cannot hold another pouch. The player sees A container cannot go in there.
  • container.contents is optional. The same list as a chest: { name = 'bread', count = 2 }. The first time that pouch is opened, those piles are packed in. After that it is a normal pouch. The player can put piles back in. Opening it again does not pack the list a second time. Dollars in that list count on the character who is carrying the pouch, the same way dollars already in a carried pouch do. A name that is not an item, a container, a mission item, the wrong category, or a pile that does not fit makes that pouch refuse to open. The server window shows the reason when the item files load.
  • A pouch always holds a count of 1. Two pouches cannot share one square, because each one has its own contents.

A picture named seed_pouch.png goes in fw_inventory/images/. A new picture shows up after ensure fw_inventory.

Give it to the player with AddItem:

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, 'herb_pouch', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

Each pouch gets its own contents the first time it is used. Two pouches are two different storages. Moving a pouch around the bag keeps the same contents.

The player opens the bag with B or /satchel, then right-clicks the pouch and chooses Open. The pouch grid appears beside the bag. They drag items in. Close on that panel hides the pouch and leaves the bag open.

Drag a pile onto the pouch picture in the bag to put the whole pile inside while the pouch stays closed. The pile fills an open pile of the same item, then the first empty square. Split it first when you want to put in less. A pouch that does not take that kind of item says That does not go in there. Another pouch says A container cannot go in there. A full pouch says Not enough room. A pile set aside for a trade stays in the bag, and the reason is That item is in a trade. Opening the pouch and dragging into its panel still works. If that pouch is already the one open beside the bag, the panel shows the pile. Any other open chest stays as it was.

A use function from RegisterUsable is skipped for a pouch. The pouch menu shows Open, and Open shows the pouch.

Using a pouch while it is sitting inside another open chest or pouch is refused. The player sees Take it out first. Put it back in the bag, then use it.

Discard throws the pouch away and deletes what was inside it. RemoveItem does the same. Moving it does not. A pouch that still holds dollars refuses with Empty the bag first. Take the dollars out first, or drop the bag. Dollars themselves refuse Discard with You cannot throw money away.

Dollars in a pouch you are carrying still count on GetCash. Dropping that pouch moves those dollars onto the pouch. They count again when someone picks the pouch up.

Drop sets the pouch on the ground in front of the player. The contents stay, and the pouch keeps the same size and the same categories. Hold Open at the bag to look inside. Hold Pick up to put it back in a satchel that has room. Anyone nearby can do either. A restart leaves the pouch where it was. Bread, ammo, and guns have Discard only. They do not get Drop. Dollars do not get Drop either. The player puts them in a money bag, then drops that bag. The reason on the dollars themselves is Put that in a bag first.

docs.title: A parcel
docs.text:
A parcel is a pouch the player only takes things out of. It is for a starter package, or anything else you hand over already packed. Give it with AddItem, the same way as any other item. This does not hand one out when a character is created. Your script does that when you want it to.

starter_parcel = {
    label = 'Starter parcel',
    category = 'container',
    width = 2,
    height = 2,
    stack = 1,
    description = 'A parcel packed for a new arrival.',
    container = {
        label = 'Starter parcel',
        width = 4,
        height = 4,
        parcel = true,
        give = false,
        contents = {
            { name = 'bread', count = 2 },
            { name = 'canned_beans', count = 2 },
            { name = 'biscuits', count = 1 },
        },
    },
}

items/container.lua already has that parcel. A picture named starter_parcel.png belongs in fw_inventory/images/.

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, 'starter_parcel', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

What you pass, on top of a pouch:

  • container.parcel = true makes it a parcel. Leave it out, or set it false, and the item is a normal pouch.
  • container.give = true lets the player give that parcel, or put it on a trade offer. Leave it out and the parcel stays with them. Give is ignored on a pouch that is not a parcel. The player sees That has to stay with you.
  • container.contents is required on a parcel. At least one { name, count }. The same rules as a pouch: a real item, not a container, not a mission item, a category the parcel accepts, and the piles have to fit. A parcel with no list, or a list that cannot be packed, refuses to open. The server window shows the reason when the item files load.

The player right-clicks the parcel and chooses Open. The piles are packed the first time. They drag what they want into the bag. Dragging something from the bag into the parcel is refused with You can only take things out of that. Moving piles around inside the parcel still works.

When the last pile leaves, the parcel is removed and the panel closes. Discard throws the parcel away while piles are still inside, and those piles are deleted with it. Dollars still inside are taken off the character. If that balance cannot be saved, the parcel stays. Drop is not on the menu. Sending a drop anyway comes back as That cannot be dropped.

A parcel with give = false has no Give. One with give = true can be handed to a nearby player, or set on a trade offer, while it still has piles. The other player opens the same parcel.

docs.title: IsReady
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes after the item list has loaded.

--- True when inventory calls can be used.
---@return boolean ready
exports.fw_inventory:IsReady()

if not exports.fw_inventory:IsReady() then
    return
end

docs.title: RegisterItem
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Adds an item type, or replaces one that already exists. The same fields as an item file, plus name. Connected players get the new definition without a restart.

--- Adds or replaces an item type.
--- False and a reason when the name or a field is rejected, or the row cannot be saved.
---@param def table
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:RegisterItem(def)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RegisterItem({
    name = 'dried_meat',
    label = 'Dried Meat',
    category = 'food',
    width = 1,
    height = 1,
    stack = 20,
    description = 'Smoked and dried. Keeps for a long time.',
})
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

A later reload from items/ updates a name that also has a file. A name that exists only from this call is left in place, because it was already written to the database the first time you registered it.

usable is true or left out. Left out means the item is not usable, so the right-click menu leaves Use off. Set usable = true when the player should see Use. RegisterUsable turns Use on as well, for as long as that callback stays registered.

context is a list of extra right-click rows. Each entry is { id = 'sharpen', label = 'Sharpen' }, or a short id string such as 'sharpen'. The id is lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, up to 32 characters, and it starts with a letter. use, open, give, drop, discard, and split are already taken. The label is the words on the row, clipped to 32 characters. Leave label out and the id is shown.

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RegisterItem({
    name = 'knife',
    label = 'Knife',
    category = 'tools',
    width = 1,
    height = 2,
    usable = true,
    context = {
        { id = 'sharpen', label = 'Sharpen' },
    },
})

When the player picks Sharpen, the server sends fw_inventory:contextOption. That message is local. Hear it with AddEventHandler. It is not queued, so the listener has to be running already. source is the player's number for this visit. item is a copy. option is the id, here sharpen.

AddEventHandler('fw_inventory:contextOption', function(source, item, option)
    if item.name ~= 'knife' or option ~= 'sharpen' then
        return
    end
end)

If the name you register, or the hash you give it, looks like a known RDR3 weapon such as WEAPON_REVOLVER_SCHOFIELD, you can leave kit, hash, width, height, and rotate out. They are filled in for you.

docs.title: RegisterUsable
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Runs your function when the player uses that item from the satchel. The item is not removed unless you call RemoveItem.

--- Registers a use callback for an item that already exists.
--- False and a reason when the item is missing or the callback is not a function.
---@param name string
---@param callback fun(source: integer, item: table)
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:RegisterUsable(name, callback)

item is a copy: id, name, label, description, count, x, y, rotated, metadata. Changing it does not change the satchel.

If your resource stops, its use callbacks are removed, and Use leaves the menu for those items unless the item itself has usable = true. Start it again and register them again.

Use is on the menu when usable is true, or when this callback is registered. Double-click uses that item too. A pouch shows Open instead, and double-click leaves the pouch closed.

exports.fw_inventory:RegisterUsable('dried_meat', function(source, item)
    local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItem(source, 'dried_meat', 1)
    if not ok then
        print(err)
    end
end)

A pouch, or any item with a container, never reaches this callback. Using it opens the pouch instead, as described in A pouch.

docs.title: GetDefinition
docs.text:
Runs on the server. A snapshot of one kind of item, or nothing when that name is not in the list. Changing what you got back does not change the list.

--- One item type, or nil when the name is unknown.
---@param name string
---@return table|nil definition
exports.fw_inventory:GetDefinition(name)

The copy can include name, label, description, width, height, stack, weapon, category, rotate, kit, hash, container, currency, image, chamber, rounds, ammo, rarity, and mission. image is the picture file in fw_inventory/images, without .png, when it is not the item name. currency is set on a pile of money, such as cash for dollars. Shops spend that balance through fw_money. category is the kind of item, such as food or tools. chamber is which rounds a gun takes, such as revolver or rifle. rounds is how many that gun holds. ammo is set on a box or a bundle of arrows. key is the game ammo name, such as AMMO_REVOLVER. fits is the same word as the gun's chamber. max is the most of that kind the character can hold. refill is how many one use adds. instant is yes for arrows, which apply as soon as they are used. rarity is uncommon, rare, epic, or legendary when the item has a colored frame. It is left out for an ordinary item. mission is yes when that item has to stay in the satchel.

local def = exports.fw_inventory:GetDefinition('herb_pouch')
if def == nil then
    return
end

docs.title: GetCatalog
docs.text:
Runs on the server. A copy of every item type, keyed by name. Same fields as GetDefinition. Changing the copy does not change the list.

--- Every item type, keyed by name.
---@return table catalog
exports.fw_inventory:GetCatalog()

local catalog = exports.fw_inventory:GetCatalog()
local rounds = catalog.ammo_revolver
if rounds == nil then
    return
end

docs.title: AddItem
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Puts items into the satchel of the character this player is playing. It finds room first. If the whole count does not fit, nothing is added.

--- Adds items to the active character's satchel.
--- False and a reason when the item is unknown, the player has no character, or it does not fit.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param count integer|nil
---@param metadata table|nil
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, name, count, metadata)

count defaults to 1. The maximum for one call is 500. Stacks that already match the name and metadata are filled first. A weapon never stacks on another weapon. A container item receives its own metadata.containerId on each new placement.

Ammo is a box, or a bundle of arrows. stack is the most of that item the satchel can hold. Giving more than that fails with You cannot carry any more of those. Using the item from the satchel puts refill rounds on the character, up to max. A box takes about two seconds. The bag stays open while the revolver-cylinder loading prompt shows at the bottom right. Backspace closes the bag. A box that is still opening is cancelled, and the box stays in the bag. Arrows apply right away. The box is not used up when the character is already at max. A shop sells one box:

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, 'ammo_revolver', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

The player uses it from the satchel. The rounds stay on the character when they log out, and they come back when that character is selected again. Draw the gun and press reload. That is on the weapons page.

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, 'rope', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

If name is not a registered item, but it looks like a known RDR3 weapon, such as weapon_revolver_cattleman, this resource creates that item type for you on the spot and then gives it. Any other unknown name fails with Unknown item. — register it first with RegisterItem or a file in items/.

docs.title: RemoveItem
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Takes that many of the name out of the satchel. If the player does not hold that many, nothing is removed. Removing a whole container placement deletes the storage that belongs to it.

--- Removes items from the active character's satchel.
--- False and a reason when the player does not hold that many.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param count integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItem(source, name, count)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItem(source, 'dried_meat', 2)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: TakeCurrency
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Takes dollars off one stack. itemId is that stack's id. storageId is the pouch when the stack is inside one you are still carrying, such as item: followed by the pouch id. Leave storageId empty when the stack is loose in the satchel. The count comes off that stack, and the character's dollar total drops by the same amount. If either change cannot be saved, neither one is kept.

A pouch on the ground, or a chest, is refused. So is a stack that is not dollars, and a stack that is sitting in a trade.

--- Takes dollars off one stack.
--- False and a reason when that stack cannot pay the count.
---@param source integer
---@param itemId string
---@param count integer
---@param storageId string|nil pouch id, or nothing when the stack is loose
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:TakeCurrency(source, itemId, count, storageId)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:TakeCurrency(source, pileId, 9, 'item:' .. pouchId)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: TakePlacement
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Takes a count off one stack that is not dollars. itemId is that stack's id. storageId is the pouch when the stack is inside one you are still carrying. Leave storageId empty when the stack is loose in the satchel. Dollars are refused. Use TakeCurrency for those, because the dollar total has to drop with the stack.

A pouch on the ground, or a chest, is refused. So is a stack that is sitting in a trade. If the stack does not hold that many, nothing is taken.

--- Takes a count off one stack that is not dollars.
--- False and a reason when that stack cannot give the count.
---@param source integer
---@param itemId string
---@param count integer
---@param storageId string|nil pouch id, or nothing when the stack is loose
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:TakePlacement(source, itemId, count, storageId)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:TakePlacement(source, pileId, 2, 'item:' .. pouchId)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: RemoveItemDeferred
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Takes that many of the name out of the satchel, the same way RemoveItem does, and the bag screen updates right away. The database write waits.

The waiting writes go out together about every five seconds. The satchel is also written when the player leaves, when the character is cleared, and when fw_inventory stops. A crash inside that wait can put the items back.

--- Removes items now and writes the satchel on the next flush.
--- False and a reason when the player does not hold that many.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param count integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItemDeferred(source, name, count)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItemDeferred(source, 'dried_meat', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: GetItems
docs.text:
Runs on the server. A snapshot of what is in the bag. You get nothing, and a reason, when the player has no character selected.

--- The placements in the active character's satchel.
---@param source integer
---@return table|nil items
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:GetItems(source)

Each placement has id, name, x, y, rotated, count, and metadata. x and y are the top-left cell. 0, 0 is the top left.

local items, err = exports.fw_inventory:GetItems(source)
if items == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: CanFit
docs.text:
Runs on the server. True when AddItem would succeed for that name and count. It does not change the satchel.

--- True when that many of the item would fit.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param count integer|nil
---@param metadata table|nil
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:CanFit(source, name, count, metadata)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:CanFit(source, 'lantern', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: PlaceAt
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Puts one new placement on an exact cell. It does not look for another spot, and it does not combine with a stack that is already sitting there.

--- Places one stack on an exact cell.
--- False and a reason when the cell is taken, outside the grid, or the item cannot turn.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param count integer|nil
---@param metadata table|nil
---@param x integer
---@param y integer
---@param rotated boolean|nil
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil idOrErr
exports.fw_inventory:PlaceAt(source, name, count, metadata, x, y, rotated)

count cannot be higher than that item's stack. On success the second value is the new placement id. That does not fit. means the rectangle is outside the grid or overlaps something else.

local ok, idOrErr = exports.fw_inventory:PlaceAt(source, 'rope', 1, nil, 0, 0, false)
if not ok then
    print(idOrErr)
    return
end

docs.title: SetGridBonus
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Adds columns or rows to the satchel under a name you choose, such as backpack. The same name replaces that bonus. It does not stack on itself. Two different names both apply. The grid cannot pass 24 by 24.

--- Adds or replaces a named size bonus on the satchel.
--- False and a reason when the key or sizes are invalid, the total would pass 24, or shrinking would cut off an item.
---@param source integer
---@param key string
---@param extraWidth integer
---@param extraHeight integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:SetGridBonus(source, key, extraWidth, extraHeight)

key is lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, up to 32 characters. 0, 0 removes that bonus.

err When Invalid bonus. key has characters outside lowercase letters, digits, and underscore, is longer than 32 characters, or extraWidth/extraHeight is not a whole number from 0 to 24. The satchel cannot grow any further. Adding this bonus on top of the base size and every other named bonus would ask for more than 24 columns or 24 rows, even though the satchel itself is capped at 24. Use a smaller bonus. Make room in the satchel first. Shrinking or removing a bonus would leave an item sitting partly off the grid. Nothing is moved. 
local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:SetGridBonus(source, 'backpack', 0, 5)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: ClearGridBonus
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Removes one named bonus. The same Invalid bonus. and Make room in the satchel first. reasons from SetGridBonus apply here.

--- Removes a named size bonus.
---@param source integer
---@param key string
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:ClearGridBonus(source, key)

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:ClearGridBonus(source, 'backpack')
if not ok then
    print(err)
end

docs.title: OpenStorage
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Opens a chest, wagon, or horse, as described in A chest, a wagon, or a horse. The first call creates it. A later call with the same name opens the same items, and can make the grid larger. The player must be playing a character.

--- Opens a storage grid for this player.
--- False and a reason when the id, size, or categories are rejected, or someone else has it open.
---@param source integer
---@param id string
---@param params table
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:OpenStorage(source, id, params)

id is the name from the chest section. params.width and params.height are the squares, from 1 to 24. params.label is the title. params.categories is the list of categories, or leave it out. params.acceptWeapons defaults to yes on this call. Pass false when this open should refuse weapons. params.contents is the same list as RegisterStorage. It is packed only when this id has no saved row yet. A later open of the same id ignores the list. A bad list comes back with the same reasons as RegisterStorage. A storage you registered should be opened with OpenRegistered instead, so the personal name, the character list, and adminOnly are applied.

err When fw_inventory is not ready The item list has not loaded yet. Ask IsReady first. Select a character first. This player is not playing a character. player is not loaded source is not a player who is in the server. Invalid storage. The name has a space, a capital letter, or some other character that is not allowed. Or params was left out. Invalid storage size. Width or height is outside 1–24. unknown category A category name is not in the list in the chest section. Invalid storage categories. params.categories was something other than a list of category names. Make room in there first. A later open tried to make the grid smaller while an item sits on a square that would disappear. Someone is using that. Another player already has this one open.

A container item cannot be placed into the storage. The player sees A container cannot go in there. Taking it back out into the bag is allowed.

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:OpenStorage(source, 'chest:valentine_1', {
    label = 'Chest',
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    categories = { 'materials', 'tools' },
})
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: CloseStorage
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Closes the second grid and leaves the satchel open. True when this player had one open. False when they did not.

--- Closes the storage this player has open.
---@param source integer
---@return boolean closed
exports.fw_inventory:CloseStorage(source)

exports.fw_inventory:CloseStorage(source)

docs.title: RegisterStorage
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Call it when your script starts. The fields are in A chest, a wagon, or a horse. The registration is dropped when your script stops. The items stay saved.

--- Remembers a storage until the calling resource stops.
--- False and a reason when the id, size, categories, character list, or locations are rejected.
---@param params table
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:RegisterStorage(params)

params.id follows the name rules in the chest section, and it must not start with item:. params.shared left out means one shared grid. params.acceptWeapons left out means weapons stay out. params.adminOnly left out means anyone can open it. params.characters left out means any character, on a shared storage. params.locations left out means no spot in the world. params.contents left out means the chest starts empty. When you pass it, the piles are packed the first time that grid is opened, as described in the chest section.

err When Invalid storage. The name is missing, too long, or starts with item:. Or params was left out. Invalid storage size. Width or height is outside 1–24. unknown category A category name is not in the list in the chest section. Invalid storage categories. params.categories was something other than a list of category names. Invalid character list. params.characters was not a list of character ids. Invalid storage locations. A spot was missing coords. Invalid storage contents. contents was not a list of { name, count }, or a count was outside 1–1000. Unknown item. A contents name is not an item. A container cannot go in there. A contents entry is itself a pouch or a parcel. That has to stay with you. A contents entry is a mission item. That does not go in there. A contents entry is a category this chest does not take. Weapons do not go in there. A contents entry is a weapon and acceptWeapons is not set. Not enough room. The piles do not fit the width and height. 
local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:RegisterStorage({
    id = 'bank:valentine',
    label = 'Safety deposit box',
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    shared = false,
    locations = {
        { coords = vector3(-308.0, 776.0, 118.0), distance = 2.0 },
    },
})
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

That box is personal. Each character gets their own items the first time they hold the prompt.

docs.title: OpenRegistered
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Opens a storage you registered. It checks the character, the character list, adminOnly, and shared, then opens the grid. The player must be playing a character.

--- Opens a registered storage for this player.
--- False and a reason when they cannot open it, or the storage was not registered.
---@param source integer
---@param id string
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:OpenRegistered(source, id)

id is the name you passed to RegisterStorage, without the :character: ending. A personal storage adds that ending for you.

err When fw_inventory is not ready The item list has not loaded yet. Ask IsReady first. Select a character first. This player is not playing a character. Finish the trade first. This player is in a trade. Invalid storage. Nothing is registered under that name, or the personal name would be longer than 64 characters. You cannot open that. adminOnly is set and this player is not an admin, or characters is set and this character is not on the list. Someone is using that. Another player already has this grid open. 
local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:OpenRegistered(source, 'bank:valentine')
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

A horse or a wagon registers with shared = false and no locations, then calls this when the player is at that horse or wagon.

docs.title: UnregisterStorage
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Removes one registration. The prompt goes away. The saved items stay, so registering the same name again opens the same chest.

--- Removes one registration. True when it was registered.
---@param id string
---@return boolean removed
exports.fw_inventory:UnregisterStorage(id)

exports.fw_inventory:UnregisterStorage('chest:valentine_1')

docs.title: PullForKit
docs.text:
Runs on the server. fw_weapons uses this when a player equips a weapon. Other scripts should use RemoveItem.

--- Takes one placement out of the satchel for a weapon slot.
--- Nil and a reason when the placement is missing or the item coming off the slot does not fit back.
---@param source integer
---@param id string
---@param displaced table|nil
---@return table|nil item
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:PullForKit(source, id, displaced)

id is the placement id from GetItems. displaced is the item leaving that weapon slot, with name, count, metadata, and rotated. It is put back on the cell that was freed. If that cell does not fit, it is placed anywhere that does. If neither works, nothing is taken and the reason is Make room in the satchel first. A placement set aside with SetHold is not taken. The reason is That item is in a trade.

docs.title: SetHold
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Marks placements that must stay in the satchel. Discard, drop, use, equip, sort, and moving one into a chest all refuse with That item is in a trade. Move and split still work on placements that are not in the list. Pass nothing, or an empty list, to clear the hold.

While any placement is held, opening a chest or a pouch comes back as Finish the trade first.

--- Marks placements that a trade is holding. Nil or an empty list clears the hold.
--- False and a reason when a listed placement is not in the satchel.
---@param source integer
---@param ids string[]|nil
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:SetHold(source, ids)

source is the player's number for this visit. ids are placement ids from GetItems. The same id twice comes back as Invalid hold.

local items = exports.fw_inventory:GetItems(source)
local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:SetHold(source, { items[1].id })
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

exports.fw_inventory:SetHold(source, nil)

docs.title: CommitTrade
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Gives each player's listed placements to the other player. Both satchels change, or neither does. The items land anywhere they fit. They do not keep the cells they had in an offer grid.

Call this only when you already know both offers are the items you mean to move. If a placement is gone, or its count or metadata changed, nothing moves and the reason is That offer changed. If the other satchel cannot hold what is coming in, nothing moves and the reason is Not enough room. or You cannot carry any more of those.

--- Swaps the listed placements between two satchels.
--- False and a reason when either offer does not match the satchel, or either satchel cannot hold what it would receive.
---@param sourceA integer
---@param sourceB integer
---@param offerA table
---@param offerB table
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_inventory:CommitTrade(sourceA, sourceB, offerA, offerB)

Each offer is a list. Each entry needs id, name, count, and metadata for one whole placement. An empty list gives nothing. sourceA and sourceB are the two players' numbers. They must be different, and both must be playing a character.

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:CommitTrade(sourceA, sourceB, offerA, offerB)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

fw_trade is the screen that locks two offers and then calls this.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text: A message on the server is heard with AddEventHandler. A message from the server to the player's game is heard with RegisterNetEvent. A message from the player's game to the server is sent with TriggerServerEvent. Your script hears one only if it is already running. Put the listener at the top of your script.

docs.title: fw_inventory:ready
docs.text:
Local, on the server. Sent once, after the item list has loaded. If your script starts later, you missed it. Ask IsReady.

AddEventHandler('fw_inventory:ready', function()
    exports.fw_inventory:RegisterUsable('dried_meat', function(source, item)
        exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItem(source, 'dried_meat', 1)
    end)
end)

fw_characters:selected loads or creates that character's bag. fw_characters:cleared saves it and forgets it. Both are messages on the server, described on fw_characters.

docs.title: fw_inventory:changed
docs.text:
Local, on the server. Sent after the satchel is saved, with the player's number for this visit (source on other pages). Hear it if your script needs that same moment.

---@param source integer
AddEventHandler('fw_inventory:changed', function(source)
    local items = exports.fw_inventory:GetItems(source)
end)

docs.title: What the bag screen sends the server
docs.text:
These are networked (RegisterNetEvent on the server, sent from the player's game with TriggerServerEvent). fw_satchel sends these when the player drags, uses, sorts, or drops. A script with its own bag screen could send them too, but for giving or taking items from your own script, use the calls above instead — AddItem, RemoveItem, and so on, not these.

token is a value you make up and send with the request. It comes back unchanged on fw_inventory:updated or fw_inventory:rejected, so a screen that fires several requests at once can tell which response answers which request. Leave it out, or pass anything, if you don't need that.

Event Parameters What it does fw_inventory:open none Opens the bag for the sender. Answered with fw_inventory:opened, or fw_inventory:rejected when the item list is not ready or the player has no character. fw_inventory:move id, x, y, rotated, token Moves a placement already in the bag to a new cell, or turns it. id is the placement id. rotated is true, false, or left out to keep its current facing. fw_inventory:sort token Rearranges the whole bag by item category, then size. fw_inventory:discard id, count, token Throws away up to count of that placement. count defaults to 1. The last one removes the placement, and deletes the container it owns, if it had one. A pouch that still holds dollars refuses with Empty the bag first. A parcel does not. Its remaining piles, including dollars, are deleted with it. fw_inventory:drop id, token Sets a pouch on the ground. id is the placement. Only an item with a container block can be dropped. A parcel cannot. The player sees That cannot be dropped. The contents of a pouch stay. That item is in a trade. is a placement set aside for a trade. fw_inventory:split id, count, token Cuts count off a stackable placement onto an empty cell of its own. count is a whole number from 1 up to one less than what is already there, and the item must be able to stack. Not enough room. means the bag has no free cell of that size. fw_inventory:use id, token, side Uses that placement, or opens a pouch. The bag sends this for Use, and for Open on a pouch. side is 'storage' when the placement is sitting in an open chest or pouch rather than the bag — that is refused with Take it out first. Opens a pouch's storage, or runs its RegisterUsable callback, or rejects with This cannot be used. Three pouches can be open at once. A fourth is refused with Close a pouch first. fw_inventory:context id, option, token The player picked a custom right-click row. id is the placement. option is the id from context on the item. That action is not on this item. means that id was not registered. That item is in a trade. means the pile is set aside. On success the server sends the local message fw_inventory:contextOption. fw_inventory:storageClose id Closes one pouch when id is that pouch. Leave id out to close every pouch the sender has open. Answered with fw_inventory:storageClosed. fw_inventory:storageMove storageId, id, x, y, rotated, token Moves a placement inside the pouch named by storageId, not the bag. id is the placement. fw_inventory:transfer fromSide, id, x, y, rotated, token, storageId, toStorageId Moves a placement between the bag and one open pouch, or from one open pouch to another. fromSide is 'satchel' or 'storage'. storageId is the pouch. When the pile moves from one open pouch onto another, storageId is the pouch it leaves and toStorageId is the pouch it lands in. fw_inventory:deposit id, containerId, token Puts the whole satchel pile id into the pouch placement containerId. The pouch can stay closed. The pile fills an open pile of the same item, then the first empty square. Not enough room. means the pouch cannot hold it. That does not go in there. means the pouch does not take that category. You can only take things out of that. means it is a parcel. A container cannot go in there. means the pile is itself a pouch. That item is in a trade. means one of the two placements is set aside. fw_inventory:openRegistered id Opens a registered storage for the sender. id is the name from RegisterStorage. Answered with fw_inventory:opened, or fw_inventory:rejected with You cannot open that. and the other reasons from OpenRegistered. The world prompt sends this. A horse script can call OpenRegistered instead. fw_inventory:requestStorageLocations none Asks for the spots that have a prompt. Answered with fw_inventory:storageLocations for the sender. fw_inventory:requestNearbyDrops none Asks which pouches are within 100 meters of the sender. Answered with fw_inventory:dropped only when that set changed. The same set gets no reply. fw_inventory:openDropped id Opens a pouch on the ground. id is the ground pouch from fw_inventory:dropped. Answered with fw_inventory:opened, or fw_inventory:rejected. That is gone. means someone already picked it up. You are too far away. means the player is not next to it. fw_inventory:pickupDropped id Puts that ground pouch into the sender's satchel when there is room. The contents come with it. Not enough room. leaves it on the ground. 
RegisterNetEvent('fw_inventory:use', function(id, token, side)
    -- fw_satchel already does this. Shown so a custom screen knows the shape.
end)

docs.title: What the server sends the bag screen
docs.text:
These are networked (RegisterNetEvent on the player's game, sent from the server with TriggerClientEvent). The screen in fw_satchel listens for these. A script with its own bag screen can listen too. Giving an item from your own script is still AddItem, not one of these.

Event Parameters What it carries fw_inventory:opened payload payload.grid is the bag. payload.definitions and payload.categories are every item type and the category names. payload.storage is the list of pouches that player has open. It is empty when none are open. fw_inventory:updated grid, token, storage The bag after a change, the token from the request that caused it (or nothing, when this page's own calls caused the change), and the list of open pouches. A pouch that left the list should come off the screen. fw_inventory:definitions definitions, categories Sent to everyone. Every item type and the category names, after RegisterItem, a reload, or a new weapon type being created automatically. fw_inventory:rejected reason, token A short reason, such as That does not go in there., and the token from the request that failed. fw_inventory:close none Hide the bag. Sent when the character is deselected, the player leaves, or this resource stops. fw_inventory:storageClosed id Hide one pouch when id is set. Hide every open pouch when id is left out. The bag stays. fw_inventory:storageLocations list Sent to one player, or to everyone, when a storage is registered or removed. Each entry has id, label, and locations. locations is { x, y, z, distance }. fw_inventory places a Hold prompt from this list. fw_inventory:dropped change The reply to the player who asked with fw_inventory:requestNearbyDrops, and only when a pouch was added or removed within 100 meters of them. change.add is one pouch, with id, label, x, y, z, and heading. change.remove is the id to stop drawing. fw_inventory draws that one bag, with Hold to open and Hold to pick up. 
RegisterNetEvent('fw_inventory:rejected', function(reason, token)
    print(reason)
end)

docs.title: Console commands
docs.text: Command Where What it does fw_items_reload Server console, or /fw_items_reload by an in-game admin Reads items/ again and re-saves every item. A player who is not an admin gets You are not an admin. in the log. An admin gets an INFO line for how many items were reloaded. fw_giveitem <serverId> <name> [count] Server console only Calls AddItem for that player. A player who types it gets a warning in the log. The server window gets the same warning. fw_gridbonus <serverId> <key> <extraWidth> <extraHeight> Server console only Calls SetGridBonus for that player. Same console-only behavior as fw_giveitem.

docs.title: State bags
docs.text: This resource does not set one. The bag screen reads fwInventoryBusy from fw_menu when a menu wants the bag kept closed.

docs.title: Item file
docs.text:
Put a Lua file in resources/[framework]/fw_inventory/items/. The file returns a map. The key is the item name: lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, up to 32 characters.

return {
    dried_meat = {
        label = 'Dried Meat',
        category = 'food',
        width = 1,
        height = 1,
        stack = 20,
        description = 'Smoked and dried. Keeps for a long time.',
    },
}
Field Default Meaning label The name Text in the satchel. Clipped to 48 characters. description empty Line in the satchel. Clipped to 200 characters. width, height Required, 1–12 How many cells the item covers before it is turned. category Required ammo, animals, documents, food, herbs, horse, medical, tools, valuables, currency, weapons, materials, or container. A pouch uses container. Dollars use currency. stack 1 How many copies share one footprint. Maximum 1000. weapon false When true, the item never stacks. rotate false The player can turn it. kit none Which weapon slot can hold it: revolver, pistol, longarm, bow, lasso, melee, lantern, binoculars, or fishingrod. hash none Weapon name, such as WEAPON_REVOLVER_CATTLEMAN. Required when kit is set. container none Opens a second grid when the player right-clicks the item and chooses Open. Stack is forced to 1. parcel, give, and contents are described in A parcel. contents on a pouch is described in A pouch. usable false true puts Use on the right-click menu. Left out, or false, leaves Use off unless RegisterUsable has a callback for this name. A pouch still shows Open. context none Extra right-click rows. A list of { id = 'sharpen', label = 'Sharpen' }, or id strings. The player’s choice arrives as fw_inventory:contextOption. ammo none A box or a bundle of arrows. key is the game ammo name, such as AMMO_REVOLVER. fits is which guns take it: revolver, pistol, repeater, rifle, elephant, shotgun, arrow, or varmint. max is the most of that kind on the character, from 1 to 999. refill is how many one use adds, and it cannot be higher than max. instant skips the open wait. Arrows set it. stack is how many of the item the satchel can hold. chamber filled in for shipped guns Which fits value this gun accepts. Set it yourself on a new gun. rounds filled in for shipped guns How many rounds that gun holds. A Cattleman is 6. A bow is 20. From 1 to 100. rarity ordinary uncommon, rare, epic, or legendary. Leave it out for an ordinary item. mission no true when the item has to stay in the satchel.

docs.title: Rarity
docs.text:
Leave rarity out and the satchel draws the plain slot. Set one of these words and the satchel, the shop, and a trade offer draw a colored frame. The same word shows under the name when the player rests on the item.

Word Frame uncommon Green rare Blue epic Purple legendary Gold

common is the same as leaving it out. Any other word is rejected. RegisterItem comes back false, and the reason is unknown rarity.

The name is the key in the item file, the same as any other item.

letter = {
    label = 'Folded Letter',
    category = 'documents',
    width = 1,
    height = 1,
    stack = 1,
    rarity = 'rare',
    description = 'The seal is still intact.',
},

mission = true is separate from the frame. The player cannot give that item, trade it, sell it, throw it away, drop it, or put it in a pouch or a chest. Leave rarity out and the frame is the gold one. Set a rarity as well when you want a different color. The card says Mission item either way.

A pouch that already holds a mission item cannot be dropped or thrown away until that item is taken out.

Another script can still take the item with RemoveItem. That is how a job finishes and collects the letter. The player cannot do that from the satchel.

rarity and mission are not columns in fw_items. They stay on the item file, and they are put back when the files load. Put them in the file when they have to survive a restart. An item that exists only from RegisterItem keeps its row, and these two fields on that call last until the next start.

warrant = {
    label = 'Arrest Warrant',
    category = 'documents',
    width = 1,
    height = 1,
    stack = 1,
    mission = true,
    description = 'It carries the court seal.',
},

Shipped guns already have chamber and rounds. You only set those two when you add a gun the list does not know. Shipped ammo is in items/ammo.lua. A revolver box adds 12, up to 200. An explosive box adds 10, and 10 is the cap. Arrows add 10, up to 40, and they apply as soon as they are used. Fire, poison, and dynamite arrows add fewer. The satchel holds 20 of any one ammo item.

If the item's name, or the hash you set, matches a known RDR3 weapon such as weapon_revolver_cattleman or WEAPON_BOW, you can leave kit, hash, width, height, and rotate out entirely — they are worked out for you from that name. The shipped items/weapons.lua sets them by hand anyway, so the shape is easy to see and change.

The picture is fw_inventory/images/<name>.png. Set image on the item file when the picture has another name. Dollars use bill_stack_single. Leave off the .png. A new picture is not served until ensure fw_inventory.

docs.title: Picture size
docs.text:
fw_satchel draws the picture inside a box sized to the item's width and height in cells, and shrinks or grows the picture to fit that box without stretching it — so a picture of roughly the right shape always looks right, even if its pixels don't match the table below exactly.

For a crisp picture at the satchel's normal size, one cell is 48 pixels, with a 2-pixel gap between cells. A footprint of n cells in one direction comes out to n * 48 + (n - 1) * 2 pixels in that direction:

width \ height 1 2 3 4 1 48x48 48x98 48x148 48x198 2 98x48 98x98 98x148 98x198 3 148x48 148x98 148x148 148x198 4 198x48 198x98 198x148 198x198

A rope, 3 wide and 1 tall, is 148x48. A herb_pouch, 2 by 2, is 98x98.

The satchel's cell can grow up to 88 pixels on a tall window, so a picture made at double the table above holds up better on a bigger screen. There's no setting for this — it's just a size to draw at.

fw_items_reload reads items/ again, as described in Console commands. This resource always loads ammo.lua, container.lua, currency.lua, food.lua, materials.lua, medical.lua, tools.lua, and weapons.lua, plus any other .lua file it finds in that folder, in alphabetical order. The file name is the list you open. Each item still has its own category. If two files define the same name, the one that sorts later wins.

docs.title: Container items
docs.text:
The walkthrough is A pouch. This is the item that ships in items/container.lua. The name is the key, so name is not repeated inside.

herb_pouch = {
    label = 'Herb Pouch',
    category = 'container',
    width = 2,
    height = 2,
    stack = 1,
    description = 'A pouch for herbs.',
    container = {
        label = 'Herb pouch',
        width = 6,
        height = 10,
        categories = { 'herbs' },
    },
}

container lives in the item file, or in the RegisterItem call. It is not a column you fill in by hand. A reload of the item files puts it back.

docs.title: Satchel screen
docs.text:
fw_satchel opens with B or /satchel. B, Escape, Backspace, or Tab closes it and releases any open storage. The gunbelt closes with the bag. A trade uses that same screen. Those same keys decline the trade. That is on fw_trade.

Drag a placement. The cells under it turn green when it fits and red when it does not. R turns it when rotate is true. Dropping a stack on the same item, with the same metadata and room left in stack, combines them. A weapon never combines.

Right-click a satchel placement for Use, Give, or Discard. A pile of more than one also offers Split in half and Split amount. Half cuts the pile in two, and an odd count leaves the extra one on the original pile. Amount is a slider from 1 up to one less than the pile. Either cut lands on an empty cell of its own. A pouch also has Drop. Dollars have no Discard. Discard throws the whole stack away. Drop sets that pouch on the ground. Give hands that whole stack to a nearby player. That is on fw_trade. Double-click uses it. If nothing registered a use callback, the line under the grid says it cannot be used.

A storage open adds a second panel to the left of the satchel, only as large as that storage's grid. The satchel and the weapon loadout stay where they are. When the loadout is open, the storage panel sits to the left of it. Close on that panel hides it and leaves the satchel open. Double-click on the storage grid is refused until the item is back in the satchel.

docs.title: fw_menu
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Open a menu on their screen. This does not know about accounts, characters, or items.

There is no code on the server. Every call on this page is an export from a client script, so call it from your own client script — not from the server.

docs.title: GetMenuData
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. This is the menu. Ask for it once, in the script that opens menus.

--- The menu for this player's game.
---@return table MenuData
local MenuData = exports.fw_menu:GetMenuData()

This is the same table fw_menu uses for itself, not a copy. Stick to the calls on this page. Other fields you might see on it are for fw_menu's own bookkeeping and can change without notice.

The same menu is also available from the message fw_menu:getData. That message stays in the player's game. Your script sends it, and passes a function. The menu calls that function with the menu table. GetMenuData is the easier way. Use the message only if you cannot call the export yet.

TriggerEvent('fw_menu:getData', function(MenuData)
    MenuData.Open('default', 'myshop', 'main', {
        title = 'Shop',
        elements = {
            { label = 'Bread', value = 'bread' },
        },
    }, function(data, menu)
        menu.close()
    end, function(data, menu)
        menu.close()
    end)
end)

docs.title: Open a menu
docs.text:
Opens a list on the player's screen. You get back a handle. The functions you pass in receive that same handle as menu.

--- Opens a menu. You get back the handle the functions below receive as menu.
---@param menuType string use 'default'
---@param namespace string your script or feature name
---@param name string menu name inside that name
---@param data table title, rows, and options
---@param submit function|nil runs with (data, menu) when the player confirms a row, or steps a slider
---@param cancel function|nil runs with (data, menu) when the player backs out
---@param change function|nil runs with (data, menu) when the highlight or a slider moves
---@param close function|nil runs with no arguments after the menu has closed
---@return table menu
MenuData.Open(menuType, namespace, name, data, submit, cancel, change, close)

menuType is default. That is the only built-in kind. Use namespace and name together so two menus do not get mixed up.

If the player closed this exact menu (same menuType, namespace, and name) before, the row they had highlighted stays highlighted the next time it opens. That memory is kept by fw_menu itself and is forgotten when fw_menu restarts, not when your own script restarts.

data:

Field Meaning title Header. subtext Line under the header. elements Rows, in order. isGrid Icon grid instead of a list. disableMovement The player cannot walk while this menu is open. Nested menus share one freeze and release it when the last one closes. lockInventory While this menu is open, the satchel should stay closed. It sets LocalPlayer.state.fwInventoryBusy to true, and back to false when the last menu that asked for this has closed.

A row:

Field Meaning label Text on the row. value What you get back when the player confirms. desc Text shown for the highlighted row. type Leave it out for a normal row. slider for a slider. min, max, hop Slider range and step. hop defaults to 1. options Labels for a slider that is not a number range. value is the index, starting at 0. image Icon name when isGrid is true.

The menu screen loads a grid icon from a fixed web path built from image, and that path points at a resource named ip-inventory (nui://ip-inventory/web/images/items/<image>.png). It is not fw_menu's own path. Grid icons only show up if something on this server is actually serving files at that address. If nothing is, the row still works — the player just sees no icon.

local MenuData = exports.fw_menu:GetMenuData()

MenuData.Open('default', 'myshop', 'main', {
    title = 'Shop',
    subtext = 'Select an item',
    disableMovement = true,
    elements = {
        { label = 'Bread', value = 'bread', desc = 'Fresh bread' },
        { label = 'Amount', type = 'slider', value = 1, min = 1, max = 10, hop = 1 },
    },
}, function(data, menu)
    print(data.current.value)
    menu.close()
end, function(data, menu)
    menu.close()
end)

A slider row is different from the other rows: moving it with Left or Right also calls your submit function right away, once per step, with data.current set to that slider row. It does not wait for the player to press Enter. If your submit function only expects a confirm value such as 'confirm', check data.current.value before acting on it, the same way the example above only closes the menu — a plain row's submit and a slider's submit both go through the same function.

docs.title: What submit, cancel, and change receive
docs.text:
The data your submit and change functions receive is not the data you gave Open. It is a small table about the one row involved:
