Field Meaning data.current The row that was confirmed or just changed — the same fields you gave it (label, value, desc, and so on), with the slider's value up to date if it is a slider. data.elements All of this menu's rows, as currently shown. Most scripts only need data.current.

cancel receives a data with neither of those — there is nothing useful to read from it. You already know which menu was cancelled, because cancel is the function you gave that menu's Open call.

MenuData.Open('default', 'myshop', 'main', shopData,
    function(data, menu) -- submit
        print('picked', data.current.value)
        menu.close()
    end,
    function(data, menu) -- cancel
        menu.close()
    end,
    function(data, menu) -- change
        print('highlighted', data.current.value)
    end
)

docs.title: Menu handle
docs.text:
The functions you passed to Open receive menu. GetOpened gives you the same kind of handle.

Call What it does menu.close() Closes this menu and runs the close function you gave Open. menu.refresh() Sends the current rows to the screen again. menu.setElement(index, key, value) Changes one field. index starts at 1. menu.setElements(elements) Replaces the row list. menu.setTitle(title) Changes the header. menu.update(query, newData) On every row whose fields match query, copies the fields from newData. menu.addNewElement(element) Adds a row. menu.removeElement(query) Removes every row whose fields match query. menu.removeElementByValue(value, stop) Removes rows with that value. stop true removes only the first. menu.removeElementByIndex(index) Removes that row. index starts at 1.

menu.data is also there to read, not just a parameter you handed in — it is the live row list fw_menu is drawing from. After a slider's change fires, its updated number is already in menu.data.elements[index].value, which is how the quantity example above could read it back. menu.type, menu.namespace, and menu.name are on the handle too, which is useful when you pulled a handle out of GetOpenedMenus() and need to tell which menu it is.

docs.title: Other calls
docs.text:
Call Returns MenuData.IsOpen(menuType, namespace, name) True when that menu is open. MenuData.GetOpened(menuType, namespace, name) The open menu, or nothing. MenuData.GetOpenedMenus() A list of open menus. MenuData.Close(menuType, namespace, name) Closes that menu. MenuData.CloseAll() Closes every open menu. MenuData.ReOpen(menu) Opens a menu that was closed, using a table from GetOpenedMenus.

fw_menu calls ReOpen on its own: if the player opens RedM's pause menu while your menu is open, fw_menu closes it, then reopens it once they leave the pause menu. You will not normally call ReOpen yourself — it is here for the rare case where you saved a handle from GetOpenedMenus() and want to bring that exact menu back.

docs.title: When the player closes the menu
docs.text:
fw_menu:closed stays in the player's game. Your script hears it only if it is already running. It has no extra information.

It is sent at the moment the player presses Backspace to back out of the menu screen — the same moment the cancel function you gave that menu runs. It is not sent when your own script closes a menu by calling menu.close(), MenuData.Close(), or MenuData.CloseAll(). Use it for something like restoring the player's cursor or HUD in general, not as a per-menu close notice — for that, use the cancel or close function you gave Open.

AddEventHandler('fw_menu:closed', function()
end)

docs.title: SetScale
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Exists to change how large the menu is drawn, with 1 meant as the normal size. In the current menu screen nothing is listening for this message yet, so calling it does not change anything the player sees today. It is safe to call — it will not error.

--- Sends a resize message to the menu screen. Has no visible effect until the menu screen listens for it.
---@param scale number
exports.fw_menu:SetScale(scale)

exports.fw_menu:SetScale(1)

MenuData.SetScale(1) is the same call after you have the menu table from GetMenuData.

docs.title: State bags
docs.text:
fwInventoryBusy is the only one. It is yes while a menu that used lockInventory is open. The bag screen should stay closed while it is yes. It is set with replication on, so the server can technically read it too, but it exists for the player's own game to check — read it client-side unless you have a specific reason not to. Set it by opening a menu with lockInventory = true. Do not set it yourself, or the bag and the menu will disagree when the menu closes.

if LocalPlayer.state.fwInventoryBusy then
    return
end

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Enter confirms the highlighted row. Backspace cancels. Up and Down move the highlight. Left and Right change a slider — and, unlike Up and Down, each press also runs that slider row through submit, not just change.

docs.title: fw_money
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Read how many dollars a player is carrying, give them dollars, or take dollars away.

The dollars are a real stack in the satchel. The number you spend is the balance stored for that character. GetCash is that balance. It counts every dollar pile in the satchel, and every dollar pile inside a pouch that is still in the satchel. Putting dollars into a pouch you are carrying does not change GetCash.

A bag on the ground keeps its own balance. A chest does too. Those dollars are not part of GetCash until someone takes them out.

One pile holds at most 500 dollars. A larger amount is several piles. AddCash fills a pile up to 500, then starts another pile. Each new pile needs an empty cell. 1,200 dollars is two piles of 500 and one of 200.

source is the player's number for this visit. An amount is a whole number of dollars. Nothing, written as nil, means the call did not do it, and the second value is the reason.

A bank is a later script. It will take these piles and keep a balance of its own.

Ask IsReady first. The server can say fw_money has started a moment before the tables are ready. Keep asking for about two minutes.

docs.title: IsReady
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes after the currency tables exist.

--- True when cash can be read and changed.
---@return boolean
exports.fw_money:IsReady()

while not exports.fw_money:IsReady() do
    Wait(100)
end

docs.title: GetCash
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The dollars this character can spend. A pouch still in the satchel counts. A bag on the ground, or a chest, does not. The first time you ask, the balance is created at 0.

Nothing when no character is selected, or the balance cannot be read.

--- The dollars this character can spend.
--- A pouch still in the satchel counts. A bag on the ground, or a chest, does not.
--- Nothing when no character is selected.
---@param source integer
---@return integer|nil amount
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_money:GetCash(source)

local dollars, err = exports.fw_money:GetCash(source)
if dollars == nil then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: AddCash
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Adds dollars to the satchel and to the balance. Fills piles up to 500, then starts another pile.

False, and nothing changes, when the satchel has no room for the new piles. The amount has to be from 1 to 100000.

--- Adds dollars to the satchel.
--- False, and nothing changes, when the new piles do not fit.
---@param source integer
---@param amount integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_money:AddCash(source, amount)

local added, err = exports.fw_money:AddCash(source, 1200)
if not added then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: RemoveCash
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Takes dollars out of the piles and lowers the balance by the same amount. Loose piles in the satchel go first. When those are not enough, it takes piles inside pouches the character is still carrying.

False, and nothing changes, when those piles and the balance are not both large enough. A bag on the ground and a chest are left alone. Dollars set aside in an open trade stay there, and the reason is That item is in a trade.

--- Takes dollars this character can spend. Loose piles go first, then a carried pouch.
--- False, and nothing changes, when the piles and the balance are not both large enough.
---@param source integer
---@param amount integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_money:RemoveCash(source, amount)

local paid, err = exports.fw_money:RemoveCash(source, 12)
if not paid then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: GetCurrency
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The same as GetCash for a named currency. cash is the one that exists now. A later currency is another item with category currency and its own name.

--- The spendable balance for one currency. Same rules as `GetCash`.
--- Nothing when no character is selected, or the name is not a currency.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@return integer|nil amount
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_money:GetCurrency(source, name)

local dollars, err = exports.fw_money:GetCurrency(source, 'cash')

docs.title: AddCurrency
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The same as AddCash for a named currency. False when no item uses that currency name.

--- Adds a currency to the satchel.
--- False, and nothing changes, when the new piles do not fit.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param amount integer
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
exports.fw_money:AddCurrency(source, name, amount)

local added, err = exports.fw_money:AddCurrency(source, 'cash', 50)

docs.title: RemoveCurrency
docs.text:
Runs on the server. The same as RemoveCash for a named currency.

--- Takes a currency this character can spend. Loose piles go first, then a carried pouch.
--- False, and nothing changes, when the piles and the balance are not both large enough.
---@param source integer
---@param name string
---@param amount integer

docs.title: What the player can do
docs.text:
The player can split a pile, give that pile, offer it in a trade, or drag it into a pouch whose categories include currency. The money bag item accepts currency. A herb pouch does not. Dragging dollars into a pouch you are carrying leaves GetCash the same. Those dollars still spend.

Drop is refused on the dollars themselves. The player puts them in a money bag, then drops the bag. The dollars stay inside that bag, and they leave GetCash. Picking the bag up puts them back.

Discard is refused on the dollars. Discard is also refused on a bag that still holds dollars. The reason is Empty the bag first. Take the dollars out, or drop the bag.

AddItem and RemoveItem on the item cash change the same balance. A counter takes the cash pile the player puts on Sell. A charge with no grid, such as the tailor, calls RemoveCash.

docs.title: Reasons you can get back
docs.text: Reason What it means Select a character first. That player has no character selected. Unknown currency. No item is marked with that currency name. Invalid amount. The amount was not a whole number from 1 to 100000. Not enough room. The satchel has no empty cell for a new pile. You do not have that much. The dollars you can spend are fewer than the amount. That item is in a trade. Those dollars are sitting in an open trade. Money is not ready. fw_money is not started. fw_money is not ready The tables are not ready yet. Ask IsReady. Could not read the cash. The balance could not be read. Could not save the cash. The balance could not be written. Nothing else was kept from that change.

docs.title: Console command
docs.text:
Command Where What it does fw_givemoney <serverId> <amount> Server window, or /fw_givemoney by an in-game admin Calls AddCash for that player. serverId is their number for this visit. amount is whole dollars, from 1 to 100000. A player who is not an admin gets You are not an admin. The server window, and that admin's console, get an INFO line when the dollars are given. fw_cash <serverId> Server window, or /fw_cash by an in-game admin Prints the dollars that player can spend. That is loose piles, plus piles in a pouch they are still carrying. A bag on the ground is not included. A player who is not an admin gets You are not an admin. The line names the character when one is selected. 
fw_givemoney 1 200
fw_cash 1

docs.title: Calls the satchel uses
docs.text:
A counter does not call these. It takes the cash pile on Sell. The satchel uses these when a pile moves between a character and a storage. The amount is the new balance, including 0.

source is not used here. characterId is fw_characters.id. storageId is the storage id from fw_inventory, such as item: plus a container id, or a chest id.

--- The character balance, without creating a row.
--- The second value is false when the row does not exist yet.
---@param characterId integer
---@param name string
---@return integer|nil amount
---@return boolean|string|nil existsOrErr
exports.fw_money:ReadCharacter(characterId, name)

--- The character balance, creating a zero row the first time.
---@param characterId integer
---@param name string
---@return integer|nil amount
exports.fw_money:EnsureCharacter(characterId, name)

--- Replaces the character balance.
---@param characterId integer
---@param name string
---@param amount integer
---@return boolean
exports.fw_money:SetCharacter(characterId, name, amount)

--- The storage balance. Zero when that storage has no row.
---@param storageId string
---@param name string
---@return integer|nil amount
exports.fw_money:GetStorage(storageId, name)

--- The storage balance, and whether a row exists.
---@param storageId string
---@param name string
---@return integer|nil amount
---@return boolean|string|nil existsOrErr
exports.fw_money:ReadStorage(storageId, name)

--- Replaces the storage balance. Zero removes the row.
---@param storageId string
---@param name string
---@param amount integer
---@return boolean
exports.fw_money:SetStorage(storageId, name, amount)

--- True when this storage still has a currency amount above zero.
--- Also true when the balance cannot be read, so a bag is not thrown away by mistake.
---@param storageId string
---@return boolean
exports.fw_money:HoldsCurrency(storageId)

--- Deletes every currency row for a storage that is being removed.
---@param storageId string
---@return nil
exports.fw_money:ForgetStorage(storageId)

The balance is written before the satchel is saved. If the satchel save fails, the previous balance is put back. The next time the character is selected, a balance that does not match the piles wins, and the piles are rebuilt in stacks of 500. When the satchel is too full to place every dollar, the bag is left as it was and the server window shows a warning.

docs.title: fw_satchel
docs.text:
Runs on the player's game. There is no code on the server. This is the bag screen. It draws the grid from fw_inventory and the loadout from fw_weapons.

It has no exports and no state bag. Give an item, open a chest, or define an item with the calls on the inventory page. Read the equipped weapons with GetKit on the weapons page. This page exists so you know which messages the screen is already listening for, and which call to use instead of sending your own.

The player opens the bag with B, or by typing /satchel. B, Escape, Backspace, or Tab closes it. Closing the bag also closes the gunbelt, and an open chest or pouch. During a trade, those same keys decline the trade instead, and the bag closes when the trade ends. That flow is on fw_trade.

Resting on a pile draws a red tile behind the picture. The switch is highlightPile in resources/[framework]/fw_satchel/shared/config.lua. true draws that tile. false leaves it off. Another script does not call this. Change the value, then restart fw_satchel.

Right-click a placement in the bag for Use, Give, Drop, or Split. Give hides the bag, shows markers on nearby players, and hands that whole stack to the one they click. The bag comes back after. Split is only there when the stack is more than one. Give is not on the menu during a trade.

docs.title: Trade screen
docs.text:
fw_trade asks this screen to show the bag with two offer grids beside it. The messages stay in the player's game. Your script should not send them. Start a trade with the prompt or /trade, described on fw_trade. /tradeui opens the same screen with nobody else in it, so you can look at the layout. Escape closes that preview.

Message What the screen does with it fw_satchel:tradeBegin Opens the bag, or switches the open bag, to the trade layout. The argument is the current trade view. fw_satchel:tradeNotice Shows a short reason under the grid. The trade stays open. fw_satchel:tradeEnd Closes the bag. fw_satchel:shopToggle Opens the counter beside the bag, or closes the bag if that counter is already open. The argument is the clerk's goods. fw_stores sends it when the player presses Shop. The bag is the one the player is carrying. fw_satchel:shopVisible The screen sends this. true means the counter is on screen. false means it just closed. Listen with AddEventHandler. It is not queued. Do not send it yourself. 
--- The counter is on screen when visible is true, and gone when it is false.
---@param visible boolean
---@return nil
AddEventHandler('fw_satchel:shopVisible', function(visible)
    -- Hide a prompt while the counter is up.
end)

Right-click a filled loadout slot for Inspect and Clean. That menu is only on the loadout, not on an item sitting in the bag. Inspect draws the gun and plays the inspect hold, then the bag closes. A knife, lasso, lantern, binoculars, bow, or fishing pole cannot be inspected. Clean does nothing yet.

The gunbelt sits on the left of those slots. Each kind on the character is an icon the size of one satchel cell, with the count in the corner. Hover an icon to read the name. A kind at zero is left off. Nothing on the belt shows Nothing on the belt. Drag a box or a bundle of arrows from the bag onto the gunbelt to load one. The gunbelt stays closed until you press its button. Closing the bag closes the gunbelt. The Kit filter on the left keeps weapons and ammo visible together.

Drag a gunbelt icon onto the satchel, or right-click it and choose Unload, to put one full box back in the bag. Those rounds come off that kind only. The bag stays open. If fewer than a full box are left, the menu says Empty. Empty clears the leftover and does not give an item. Dragging a short stack onto the satchel shows Not a full box. and leaves the rounds in place. If the bag cannot hold the box, nothing changes and the player sees You cannot carry any more of those.

Use an ammo box or a bundle of arrows from the bag. That puts rounds on the character. The bag stays open. A box shows the revolver-cylinder loading prompt at the bottom right for about two seconds. Backspace closes the bag. A box that is still opening is cancelled, and the box stays in the bag. Draw the gun and press reload. Firing spends those rounds. The bag is not charged again. That is on fw_weapons. Inspect uses Inspect on that same page. Read the belt with GetBelt on that page.

fwInventoryBusy on fw_menu is how another menu asks this screen to stay closed.

docs.title: The command
docs.text: /satchel is a client command, typed in chat or the console. It toggles the screen: closed if open, otherwise it asks the server to open it. It takes no arguments and gives nothing back. A script should not run it for the player — trigger the underlying calls on fw_inventory instead, as shown below.

docs.title: Messages the screen uses
docs.text:
These go between the bag screen and the server. A new script should use the call named in the last column instead of sending or listening for the message itself. Sending the screen's own message skips the checks that call already does, or fights the screen for the same drag.

Message here means a networked event — sent with TriggerServerEvent or TriggerClientEvent, heard with RegisterNetEvent. Your script hears one only if it is already running when the message is sent. A script that starts after the message went out missed it; there is no queue to catch up on later.

docs.title: From the server to the player's game
docs.text:
Heard with RegisterNetEvent. These are sent by fw_inventory and fw_weapons, not by this resource.

Message What the screen does with it What you should use fw_inventory:opened Shows the bag, and a chest or pouch when one was opened. OpenStorage fw_inventory:updated Redraws the bag after a move. AddItem, RemoveItem, GetItems fw_inventory:definitions Learns item names, sizes, and pictures. RegisterItem, GetDefinition fw_inventory:rejected Shows the reason under the grid. Read the reason your call returned fw_inventory:close Hides the bag. Let the player close it fw_inventory:storageClosed Hides one pouch when the message includes its id, or every open pouch when it does not. The bag stays up. CloseStorage fw_weapons:updated Redraws the loadout. GetKit fw_weapons:rejected Shows why an equip failed. Read fw_weapons:rejected on the weapons page

fw_inventory:storageClosed is the one a script that draws its own chest panel would listen for:

RegisterNetEvent('fw_inventory:storageClosed', function(id)
    -- id is one pouch. Nothing means every open pouch closed. The bag screen already hides them.
end)

docs.title: From the player's game to the server
docs.text:
Sent with TriggerServerEvent. The bag screen is the thing that sends these, in response to the player dragging or clicking in the UI. A script building its own panel should call the matching export on fw_inventory or fw_weapons instead of sending the message directly — the export does the same validation the screen relies on.

Message What it does What you should use fw_inventory:open Asks the server for the bag. The player presses B or types /satchel fw_inventory:move Moves an item inside the bag. The player drags it fw_inventory:storageMove Moves an item inside one open pouch. The first value is that pouch's id. The player drags it fw_inventory:transfer Moves an item between the bag and a pouch, or from one open pouch to another. The player drags it across fw_inventory:deposit Puts a whole pile into a pouch in the bag. The pouch can stay closed. The pile needs a free square inside, or room on an open pile of the same item. The player drags the pile onto the pouch picture fw_inventory:use Uses the item. A pouch opens. Anything else runs RegisterUsable. RegisterUsable, or the pouch's container block fw_inventory:discard Drops part or all of a stack. RemoveItem fw_inventory:split Cuts some off a pile onto an empty square of its own. The player chooses Split in half, or Split amount fw_inventory:sort Packs the bag. The player chooses sort fw_inventory:storageClose Closes one pouch when an id is sent, or every open pouch when it is not. The bag stays open. CloseStorage fw_weapons:equip Puts a bag item onto a weapon slot. See fw_weapons fw_weapons:unequip Puts a weapon slot back in the bag. See fw_weapons fw_weapons:move Swaps two weapon slots. See fw_weapons

A shop that hands the player a rope does this. It does not send fw_inventory:move, and it does not open the bag:

local ok, err = exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, 'rope', 1)
if not ok then
    print(err)
    return
end

docs.title: Clothing while the bag is open
docs.text: The bag screen also shows a row of worn clothing (hat, coat, gloves, and so on) so the player can toggle a piece on or off without leaving the screen. It reads and changes that through fw_clothing's own exports. There is nothing here for another script to call — if you need to read or change what a character is wearing, use fw_clothing directly.

docs.title: fw_stores
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Walk up to the clerk during open hours and press G. A short loading prompt plays while the counter is gathered, then the counter opens. Press Escape, or press Close, to leave it. Pressing Shop again closes it too.

Closing the counter puts the shelf back the way the store lists it. What you settled stays in your bag.

The clerk's goods are their own panel on the left, in the same journal style as the bag. Want and Offer are two panels between them and the bag. Want is what you are asking the clerk for. Offer is what you are putting up. None of those panels can be dragged. The bag on the right is the one you are carrying. Right-click, drag, split, use, give, and drop work the same way they do when you open the bag on its own. So do the pictures on the left of the bag, the clothes, the kit, and the gunbelt. The clerk keeps one pile of each thing. A pile with a number is a limited stock, and that number goes down when you buy it. A pile with no number is always in stock. Drag a pile into Want and choose how many. Canned beans from tier I can be up to 20 in one purchase. A hatchet is one, and a shovel is one. Those are as many as one pile in the satchel can hold. The rest of a limited pile stays on the counter. Shift-click a pile to move all of it onto Want or Offer. When Want already holds a purchase, Shift-click on dollars moves only the price still owed, and Shift-click on the trade goods moves only how many that purchase still needs. Otherwise Shift-click moves the whole pile. Ctrl-click moves 10. A counter pile that does not run out has no whole pile, so Shift does nothing there and Ctrl still takes 10. Click a pile on Want or Offer to put that whole pile back. Drag a pile from your bag into Offer. A pile the clerk does not buy is grey, in the bag and in an open pouch, and it will not move onto Offer. Dollars still move. So does something the clerk buys, and something that pays for a trade once you are trusted enough. A pile in an open pouch can go there too when the clerk takes it. The pile stays where it was. Drag a pile back out of Want to return it to the counter, or out of Offer to take it back. A counter pile will not sit in Offer, and a bag pile will not sit in Want.

Gold numbers are what you pay. A number with a plus is what the clerk pays you. You pay with a dollars pile on Offer. Drag Dollars from your bag, or from an open pouch, onto Offer. The count is how many dollars you are putting up, and that many leave the stack right then. The amount under Offer is the dollars sitting there. Settle spends the price and puts the rest back in the bag. Drag those dollars off Offer, or close the counter, and they come back too. What you put on Offer that the clerk buys is taken out of the bag. What you put on Want is placed in the bag. If the clerk owes you, those dollars are placed in the bag. A tin of beans is 5 dollars at Worths in Valentine and 4 dollars in the other towns. Put dollars on Offer to buy it. A sack of flour is 10 dollars. A hatchet is 80 dollars, and it stays locked until you are established with the clerk. Worths also sells a loaf of bread for 2 dollars. The clerk buys an egg for 2 dollars at Worths and 1 dollar in the other towns, once you are recognized. An apple, a potato, or an ear of corn is 1 dollar. A bundle of mint is 2 dollars. A jar of honey, a block of beeswax, a bundle of wool, a rabbit pelt, or a fish is 4 dollars. A deer hide is 8 dollars. On this visit everyone is unknown, so the counter takes dollars and does not buy goods.

On the left of the clerk's goods are the same round pictures as the bag. All shows every pile. Kit shows weapons and ammo together. Each other picture shows that one kind, such as food, medical, or containers. A pile that does not match goes grey and stays where it is. Press that picture again, or press All, to show every kind. Want and Offer are not filtered. The bag has its own pictures, the same ones you use when the counter is closed.

Above the clerk's goods is a mark of four small squares, then I, II, III, and IV. I is Unknown, II is Recognized, III is Trusted, and IV is Established. The four squares show every pile, packed to the top of the counter. A numeral shows only that standing, packed the same way. You can press a numeral up through your own standing. A higher one stays grey. With reputation off, every visit is Unknown, so I can be pressed, and II, III, and IV stay grey. A pile above your standing is locked on the full counter and cannot be bought. A tin of peaches is II. The counter scrolls when the shelf is taller than the page.

Goods, Work, and Services switch only the clerk's panel. Want, Offer, and the satchel stay where they are. Work says the clerk has no errand on this visit. Services says they are not mending or treating anyone on this visit.

docs.title: Opening the counter
docs.text:
Pressing Shop at the clerk opens that store, after a short loading prompt while the visit is built. That pause is openPauseMs on FwStoresConfig, 400 milliseconds unless you change it. The Shop prompt hides while that counter is on screen, and comes back when it closes. Start fw_stores after fw_satchel and fw_inventory, because the screen uses their pictures and the bag.

Another script on the player's game can open a named store. storeId is the store name, such as ValentineGeneral or BlackwaterGeneral. A missing name does nothing. The counter closes if that event runs again while it is already open.

--- Opens one store's counter beside the bag.
--- Nothing happens when that store is missing, or when the name is empty.
---@param storeId string
---@return nil
AddEventHandler('fw_stores:open', function(storeId)
    -- The bag screen keeps the mouse.
end)

TriggerEvent('fw_stores:open', 'ValentineGeneral')

docs.title: The store list
docs.text:
Write stores in resources/[framework]/fw_stores/shared/config.lua. A type is the kind of shop, such as general. A store is one counter of that type. Set type = 'general' on the store.

A store is a named field on StoresConfig. That same table is FwStoresConfig.stores. The name is how you read one store.

StoresConfig.BlackwaterGeneral.blip
StoresConfig.BlackwaterGeneral.goods
StoresConfig.BlackwaterGeneral.access

A type on FwStoresConfig.types is one kind of shop. general is the first. A new kind is another entry there: a label, a template name, a scenario, lines, a mark, and who may trade. A store that names that type receives those fields.

Write type, name, location, model, voice, and hours on the store. type is the kind, such as general. name is the words on the map mark. hours belongs to this shop and is not taken from the type. Leave template, scenario, lines, takes, blip, access, pay, buy, and rows off and the store uses its type. Write one of those fields when this shop should differ. A field you write replaces that field for this shop. A blip field you write replaces that one field, and the rest of the mark stays with the type. template = false skips the type's shelf and keeps only the goods and buyback written on this store.

rows on a type is how many rows that counter uses. Leave it off and the counter stays at counter.rows, which is 14. The gunsmith sets 20 so a rifle still packs. Raising the shared 14 would add empty rows to the general store. A store can write rows when that one shop should differ.

Leave pay and buy off a type and that shop uses the general rates. Write them on the type when that trade should differ. access.sell set to a word that is not a standing, such as Closed, means the clerk never buys. The gunsmith is set that way. The butcher, the trapper, and the bait shop set sell to Unknown, so a first visit can still sell. The doctor and the saloon keep selling at Recognized, the same as the general store. Barter stays closed on these shelves until a type has a real trade.

goods and buyback are the shelf. access says who may buy, sell, and barter. pay is the share of the shelf price. buy is the share of the buyback. StoresConfig.BlackwaterGeneral.access matches the general type until Blackwater writes its own.

The general type sets template to general, the shelf in shared/templates.lua. Then list only what differs. A line whose item is already on the template changes only the fields you write. A new item is added to that store alone. A buyback name you write replaces that price. A new name is added. One town's price does not change the template or another town.

Worths does that. The tin of beans stays on the shelf and becomes 5 dollars. Bread is not on the template, so Worths alone sells it, for 2 dollars. An egg buyback of 2 replaces the template price of 1. Keane's Saloon does the same kind of change for one drink: whiskey there is 8 dollars, and the rest of the saloon shelf stays as written.

ValentineGeneral = {
    type = 'general',
    name = 'Worths General Store',
    location = vector4(-324.16, 803.62, 117.88, 272.93),
    model = 'u_m_m_valgenstoreowner_01',
    voice = '0478_U_M_M_VALGENSTOREOWNER_01',
    hours = false,
    goods = {
        { item = 'consumable_can_beans', price = 5 },
        { item = 'consumable_bread', price = 2 },
    },
    buyback = {
        egg = 2,
    },
}

The other general stores, in Strawberry, Saint Denis, Armadillo, Rhodes, Blackwater, Tumbleweed, and Wallace Station, keep the general type's shelf.

location is where the clerk stands, a vector4 with the heading last. hours is written on that store. It is { open, close } or false. The first hour is included and the second is not, so { 6, 21 } is 6:00 through 20:59. When the first hour is later, such as { 21, 6 }, the shop stays open across midnight. false means always open. The general stores are open all day. Outside the hours you write, the clerk is gone, the Shop prompt is hidden, and a sale is refused with The store is closed. If the time resource is not running, the shop stays open.

model is the ped. scenario is the stance, such as WORLD_HUMAN_SHOPKEEPER. voice is that ped's voice bank. lines names the greet, the browse line when the counter opens, and the sale line when the trade goes through. takes is how many recordings a line has. A sale picks one of those and cuts off a line already playing.

The clerk appears within spawnDistance (50) while the shop is open. The prompt is within promptDistance (2.5). Each store's blip.range decides when its mark is on the map. blipRange (120) is that distance when a store does not set its own.

blip is that store's mark. Leave it off and the store uses its type's mark. The name on the store is the words on that mark. style is the blip style, such as BLIP_STYLE_DEBUG_YELLOW. sprite is the icon, such as blip_ambient_npc. modifiers is a list of blip modifiers, such as BLIP_MODIFIER_MP_COLOR_6. color is a color word, such as yellow, when you are not listing modifiers. range is how close the player must be, in metres, before the mark exists. The general type's mark uses 150. The mark stays until the player is 20 metres past that, then it leaves the map. Come back inside the range and it returns. Leave range off a mark you write yourself and the store uses blipRange (120).

docs.title: fw_trade
docs.text:
Runs on the server and in the player's game. Two players trade what is in their satchels. The bag screen from fw_satchel draws it. This page is how a trade starts, how the two offers lock, and how the items move.

Money is not part of a trade. A gun on the belt is not in the satchel, so it is not part of a trade either. Put it in the bag first. That is on fw_weapons.

docs.title: Starting a trade
docs.text:
Stand within about 8 meters of the other players. Hold the interact control (the same one a clothing shop uses) and the prompt says Offer trade. Typing /trade does the same thing.

That opens markers on the nearby players. Click the person you want. Escape cancels and nothing is offered. Someone in another building does not get a marker. Up to 8 people nearby can show at once.

The other player gets a prompt, {Name} wants to trade. Hold to open it. Press the other control to decline. The prompt lasts about 20 seconds. If it runs out, both players see The trade offer expired.

The name is the character's first and last name. source on this page is the player's number for this visit. nil means nothing came back.

Type /tradeui to open this screen by yourself. Your satchel is on the right. Their offer fills with copies of what is already in your bag, so you can see that grid. Drag into your offer, then lock it. Accept turns on, and clicking it does not move anything. Escape, Decline, or /tradeui again closes it.

A trade does not start when either player is already trading, dead, or not playing a character. The player who offered it then sees a short reason, such as They are too far away. or They are already trading.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
Both players see the same bag screen.

  • The right side is their own satchel.
  • Your offer is the top grid on the left. It is 10 cells across and 5 down. Drag a whole placement up from the satchel. Drag it back to take it out of the offer. The placement stays in the satchel until the trade is accepted, and it still takes up its old space there.
  • Their offer is the bottom grid. It stays empty, with They have not locked an offer., until the other player locks.
  • Decline trade is there for both players the whole time. B, Escape, Backspace, or Tab does the same thing. Both screens close and nothing moves.
  • Accept trade is only on the screen of the player who offered the trade.

Lock offer shows your grid to the other player and stops you from dragging. Unlock offer hides it again and turns Accept off. You cannot drag while you are locked. Unlock first, then change the offer.

Accept stays dim until both offers are locked. The other player never gets an Accept button. They see Waiting for them to accept. once both are locked. If either player unlocks, Accept turns off again.

The offer grids only hold what fits in 10 by 5. A placement that does not fit stays in the satchel, and the player sees That does not fit.

Drop, use, equip, and sort will not take a placement that is in an offer. The player sees That item is in a trade. Move and split still work on what is left in the bag, so a stack can be split and then dragged in. A pouch cannot be opened while the trade screen is up. The reason is Finish the trade first.

docs.title: When it finishes
docs.text:
Accept gives each locked offer to the other satchel. A pouch keeps what is inside it, because that stays with the pouch. The items land in the first open cells. They do not keep the cells from the offer grid.

If the other satchel cannot hold what is coming in, both players stay on the trade screen and see There is no room for that in the satchel. Nothing is taken.

The trade also ends, and nothing moves, when someone walks farther than about 12 meters away, dies, leaves, or drops their character. Both players see a short reason, such as You walked too far apart.

docs.title: Giving an item
docs.text:
Right-click a placement in the satchel and choose Give. The bag hides, the same markers come up, and you click who receives it. The whole stack moves. There is no trade screen and they do not have to accept. Split the stack first when you want to hand over only part of it.

Both players get a line in the log, such as You gave Rope to {Name}. and {Name} gave you Rope. The same log is where a failure shows up, such as They have no room for that. Open the client console with F8 to read it. The server window shows that same line, with the player's number for this visit.

Nothing moves, and you see a short reason, when they are too far away, already trading, or their satchel has no room. You see They have no room for that. in that last case. You also cannot give while you are already in a trade. The reason is Finish the trade first.

Escape on the markers puts the bag back and leaves the item where it was.

docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Shows the nearby-player markers and waits until they click one, or cancel. The player's number for this visit comes back. Nothing comes back when they cancel, nobody is close enough, or the markers are already up.

--- The server id of the player they clicked. Nothing when they cancel.
---@return integer|nil serverId
exports.fw_trade:SelectPlayer()

local serverId = exports.fw_trade:SelectPlayer()
if serverId == nil then
    return
end

Call it from the player's game, not the server. It takes the mouse until they click or press Escape. Do not call it while another menu already has the mouse.

docs.title: IsInTrade
docs.text:
Runs on the server. Yes when this player has the trade screen open. No during the prompt before that, and no when they are not trading.

--- True when this player has the trade screen open.
---@param source integer
---@return boolean
exports.fw_trade:IsInTrade(source)

if exports.fw_trade:IsInTrade(source) then
    print('Finish the trade first.')
    return
end

The swap itself is CommitTrade on fw_inventory. SetHold on that page is how an offer stays in the satchel until Accept. Another script should not call those to finish a trade of its own unless it is running the same lock rules. This resource already does.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
A message on the server is heard with AddEventHandler. A message from the server to the player's game is heard with RegisterNetEvent. A message from the player's game to the server is sent with TriggerServerEvent. Your script hears one only if it is already running. Put the listener at the top of your script.

These are sent by this resource's own screen. Do not send them from another script. That skips the distance check, or fights the two players for the same trade.

docs.title: From the player's game to the server
docs.text: Message What it does fw_trade:request Offers a trade to the player number they clicked. fw_trade:give Hands one whole placement to that player. The arguments are their player number and the placement id. The bag screen sends this after Give. fw_trade:respond The other player accepts (true) or declines (false) the prompt. fw_trade:offer Replaces that player's unlocked offer. The argument is a list of { id, x, y, rotated }. fw_trade:lock true locks the offer. false unlocks it. fw_trade:accept The player who started the trade finishes it. Refused until both offers are locked. fw_trade:decline Either player cancels. Nothing moves. fw_trade:abort The player's game reports that someone walked too far or died. The server checks the distance and whether they are dead before it ends the trade.

docs.title: From the server to the player's game
docs.text:
Message What it carries fw_trade:waiting The other character's name, while the prompt is up. fw_trade:invited { from, name } for the player who was offered the trade. from is that other player's number. fw_trade:inviteClosed A short reason. The trade screen does not open. fw_trade:state The current view: whether you started it, the other name, both lock flags, your offer, and their offer once they have locked. fw_trade:notice A short reason while the screen stays open, such as There is no room for that in the satchel. fw_trade:closed A short reason. The bag closes. fw_trade:rejected A short reason when the offer never started. 
RegisterNetEvent('fw_trade:closed', function(reason)
    print(reason)
end)

docs.title: fw_weapons
docs.text:
Runs on the server and in the player's game. This is the weapon kit: the guns and tools the character has equipped, separate from the bag.

The bag still holds the item. Equipping takes it out of the bag and puts it on a slot. Unequipping puts it back.

The slots are revolver_1 (right revolver), revolver_2 (left revolver), longarm, bow, lasso, knife, lantern, binoculars, and fishingrod (fishing pole).

A sidearm needs a gunbelt, and so does the knife. The left revolver also needs the offhand holster, and the right revolver has to be filled first. Dragging a gun onto the empty left slot shows Equip the right revolver first. Taking the right revolver off while the left one is still there shows Take the left revolver off first. fw_weapons reads the belt and holster from fw_clothing. If the gunbelt comes off, the right revolver, the left revolver, and the knife all go back to the bag. If just the offhand holster comes off, only the left revolver goes back. If the bag is full, the player sees Make room in the satchel first.

source on this page is the player's number for this visit. Nothing is written as nil.

docs.title: GetKit
docs.text:
Runs on the server. A snapshot of the kit for the character this player is playing. You get nothing when this player has not selected a character yet, when the kit is still loading right after they did, or when fw_weapons itself has not started yet. Changing the snapshot does not save.

--- The equipped slots, or nothing when this player has no kit yet.
---@param source integer
---@return table|nil kit
exports.fw_weapons:GetKit(source)

Each slot is false when it is empty. When it holds something, it has name, count, metadata, hash, kit, and rotated. name is the item name. kit is the kind of slot it belongs on, such as revolver or melee.

A sheriff script can refuse to start a duel when the player has no sidearm:

local kit = exports.fw_weapons:GetKit(source)
if kit == nil or kit.revolver_1 == false then
    return
end
print(kit.revolver_1.name)

docs.title: GetKit
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The same snapshot, for the local player.

--- The equipped slots on this player's game.
---@return table kit
exports.fw_weapons:GetKit()

Before the server has sent a kit, this can be an empty table with no slot keys at all yet, not a table where every slot is false. Check with type(...) == 'table' rather than only ~= false, so you don't try to read a field off nothing:

local kit = exports.fw_weapons:GetKit()
if type(kit.longarm) == 'table' then
    print(kit.longarm.name)
end

docs.title: GetBelt
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. The rounds on this character. One row for each kind above zero. count includes rounds already in a gun. max is the most of that kind the character can hold. refill is how many rounds make one full box. An empty list means the belt is empty. The list is only the kinds above zero, so a kind you have used up is not in it.

The bag draws this on the gunbelt next to the loadout.

--- Rounds on this character. One row for each kind above zero.
---@return table rows
exports.fw_weapons:GetBelt()

local belt = exports.fw_weapons:GetBelt()
for index = 1, #belt do
    print(belt[index].key, belt[index].count, belt[index].max, belt[index].refill)
end

docs.title: Inspect
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. Draws the gun in that loadout slot and plays the inspect hold. The bag closes first, so the player can see it. You get no when that slot is empty, when the thing in it is not a gun, or when an inspect is already playing.

A knife, lasso, lantern, binoculars, bow, or fishing pole cannot be inspected this way. Clean is on the same right-click menu, and it does nothing yet.

--- Draws the gun in this loadout slot and plays the inspect hold.
--- False when the slot is empty, the weapon is not a gun, or an inspect is already playing.
---@param slotId string
---@return boolean started
exports.fw_weapons:Inspect(slotId)

slotId is a loadout slot name, such as revolver_1 or longarm. The right-click menu on a filled loadout slot calls this for Inspect.

local started = exports.fw_weapons:Inspect('revolver_1')
if not started then
    return
end

docs.title: fw_weapons:updated
docs.text:
Local event in the player's game, raised with TriggerEvent and heard with AddEventHandler. Sent after the kit on this computer changes, including the first time it arrives from the server. kit is a snapshot. Ask GetKit when you need a fresh one.

    if kit.longarm ~= false then
        print(kit.longarm.name)

end)

docs.text:
Networked event, sent from the server to the player's game with TriggerClientEvent and heard there with RegisterNetEvent. This is the kit they should show. fw_weapons already applies it and then sends fw_weapons:updated. Listen here only if you are drawing your own loadout.

---@param kit table

end)

docs.title: fw_weapons:rejected
docs.text:
Networked event, sent from the server to the player's game with TriggerClientEvent and heard there with RegisterNetEvent. reason is a short line. The satchel shows it. Listen here if your own screen should show that line.

---@param reason string
RegisterNetEvent('fw_weapons:rejected', function(reason)
    print(reason)
end)

This is sent whenever fw_weapons:wear, fw_weapons:equip, fw_weapons:unequip, or fw_weapons:move (described below) could not be done, when an ammo box or a bundle of arrows could not be used, and when rounds could not be taken off the gunbelt. The possible lines are:

Reason When Select a character first. This player is not playing a character. The kit is still loading. A character was just selected and the saved kit has not finished loading yet. Try again shortly. That item is not in the satchel. The placement id passed to fw_weapons:equip is not in the bag. That does not fit there. The slot name is not one of the nine listed above, or the item's kit does not match the slot it was aimed at. That slot is empty. fw_weapons:unequip or fw_weapons:move named a slot that has nothing on it. Put on a gunbelt first. revolver_1, revolver_2, or knife was used with no gunbelt worn. Put on another holster first. revolver_2 was used with no offhand holster worn. Equip the right revolver first. The left slot would end up holding a gun while the right slot stays empty. Take the left revolver off first. The right slot would be cleared while the left slot still holds a gun. Make room in the satchel first. The bag has no space for the item that needs to go back into it. The kit is busy. Another equip, unequip, or move for this player has not finished yet. Try again shortly. Could not save the kit. The database could not store the change. Rare. The action did not happen. You cannot carry any more of that ammunition. Using an ammo box or arrows would go past the carry limit for that kind. The item stays in the satchel. That box is gone. The ammo item was no longer in the satchel when the use finished. You cannot carry any more of those. Unloading a full box would not fit in the satchel. The rounds stay on the character. Not a full box. A short remainder was dragged back onto the satchel. The rounds stay. Choose Empty on the icon to clear them.

docs.title: fw_weapons:wear
docs.text:
Networked event, sent from the player's game to the server with TriggerServerEvent and heard there with RegisterNetEvent. fw_weapons sends it itself when the gunbelt or the offhand holster changes. belt and offhand are yes or no.

Another script should not send this. Change the clothes with fw_clothing. The kit follows.

---@param belt boolean
---@param offhand boolean
TriggerServerEvent('fw_weapons:wear', belt, offhand)

docs.title: fw_weapons:equip
docs.text:
Networked event, sent from the player's game to the server with TriggerServerEvent and heard there with RegisterNetEvent. The satchel sends this when the player drops a bag item onto a loadout slot.

placementId is the id from GetItems. slotId is one of the slot names above. The item's kit field has to match that slot. A revolver goes on revolver_1 (the right hip) or revolver_2 (the left hip). The right slot has to already hold a gun before the left slot will take one. revolver_1, revolver_2, and knife all need a gunbelt worn first, and revolver_2 also needs the offhand holster. A rifle goes on longarm. A fishing pole goes on fishingrod. The item name for the shipped pole is weapon_fishingrod, and its kit is fishingrod.

If it fails, the player's game gets fw_weapons:rejected with one of the reasons listed above.

---@param placementId integer
---@param slotId string
TriggerServerEvent('fw_weapons:equip', placementId, slotId)

A camp script can put the cattleman already in the bag onto the hip:

local items = exports.fw_inventory:GetItems(source)
for index = 1, #items do
    if items[index].name == 'weapon_revolver_cattleman' then
        TriggerClientEvent('my_camp:equip', source, items[index].id)
        break
    end
end

In the player's game, after that message:

RegisterNetEvent('my_camp:equip', function(placementId)
    TriggerServerEvent('fw_weapons:equip', placementId, 'revolver_1')
end)

Giving a weapon the player does not already hold is AddItem on fw_inventory. They equip it from the loadout after that.

docs.title: fw_weapons:unequip
docs.text:
Networked event, sent from the player's game to the server with TriggerServerEvent and heard there with RegisterNetEvent. Puts that slot back into the bag.

slotId is the slot name. It has to already hold something, and taking the right revolver off while the left one is still in place is refused with Take the left revolver off first. x and y are the bag square to aim for, with 0, 0 at the top left. rotated turns the item if that item can turn. If that square does not fit, the item is placed anywhere that does. If the bag cannot take it, nothing moves, and the reason is Make room in the satchel first.

---@param slotId string
---@param x integer
---@param y integer
---@param rotated boolean
TriggerServerEvent('fw_weapons:unequip', 'knife', 0, 0, false)

docs.title: fw_weapons:move
docs.text:
Networked event, sent from the player's game to the server with TriggerServerEvent and heard there with RegisterNetEvent. Swaps two slots.

fromId and toId both have to be real slots, and each cannot be empty. The item leaving fromId has to be allowed on toId, and if toId already holds something, that item has to be allowed back on fromId too — a swap only goes through when both items fit both ways. Moving into revolver_1, revolver_2, or knife needs the same gunbelt (and, for revolver_2, offhand holster) as equipping does.

---@param fromId string
---@param toId string
TriggerServerEvent('fw_weapons:move', 'revolver_1', 'revolver_2')

Swaps the two revolvers when both slots already hold a gun. Moving the right revolver onto an empty left slot is refused with Equip the right revolver first.

docs.title: Ammo
docs.text:
Ammo in the satchel is a box, or a bundle of arrows. It is not the clothing gunbelt. Using it from the satchel puts rounds on the character. A box takes about two seconds. The bag stays open, and the revolver-cylinder loading prompt shows at the bottom right. Backspace closes the bag. A box that is still opening is cancelled, and the box stays in the bag. Arrows apply right away. If that kind is already at its limit, the item is not used, and the player sees You cannot carry any more of that ammunition.

Those rounds stay on the character. Firing and reloading spend them. The satchel is not charged again. Two guns that take the same rounds, such as two Cattlemen, share that pool. The count is saved on the character and put back the next time that character is selected. The bag shows the kinds above zero on the gunbelt, next to the loadout. Read that list with GetBelt.

To take rounds off, drag that kind's icon from the gunbelt onto the satchel, or right-click it and choose Unload. One full box goes back into the bag, and those rounds come off. The box comes back right away, and the bag stays open. If the bag cannot hold that box, nothing changes, and the player sees You cannot carry any more of those.

Each kind has its own limit. Taking express revolver rounds off frees room for more express rounds. It does not raise the limit on regular revolver rounds. When a kind hits zero it drops off the weapon wheel and off the gunbelt.

If fewer than a full box are left, the menu says Empty. Empty clears the leftover and does not give an item, so a half-used box cannot be turned back into a full one. Dragging a short stack onto the satchel shows Not a full box. and leaves the rounds in place. Right-click Empty is how that kind is cleared.

The satchel sends the ammo type, not a count. Leave this call to the bag screen.

---@param ammoType string
---@param empty boolean
TriggerServerEvent('fw_weapons:unload', 'AMMO_REVOLVER', false)

ammoType is the game ammo name, such as AMMO_REVOLVER. empty is yes only for the Empty choice. A drag sends no. A box comes back when a full box of that kind is on the character and the bag can hold it. Those rounds then come off. Empty clears a short remainder and gives nothing.

A shop gives a box with AddItem, on the inventory page. One revolver box adds 12 rounds, up to 200. The player uses the box, draws the gun, and presses reload.

There is no call on this page for loading a gun by hand.

docs.title: State bags
docs.text: This resource does not set one. Read the kit with GetKit.

docs.title: Tutorial: a crafting resource
docs.text:
This builds one resource, fw_crafting, from nothing. A player types /craft and, if they are carrying 3 Plant Fiber, it becomes 1 Rope. One recipe, kept small on purpose. The patterns here are the same ones you would use for ten recipes, or for giving items from any other kind of resource.

Read Write a script first if you have not. This tutorial is that pattern, with a real feature built on top of it.

docs.title: What it needs running first
docs.text:
fw_crafting calls fw_core, fw_characters, and fw_inventory, and uses vorp_lib for logging. All four have to already be in server.cfg above it:

ensure vorp_lib
ensure fw_core
ensure fw_characters
ensure fw_inventory
ensure fw_crafting

docs.title: The folder
docs.text:
resources/[framework]/fw_crafting/
    fxmanifest.lua
    client/main.lua
    server/main.lua

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
fx_version 'cerulean'
game 'rdr3'

rdr3_warning 'I acknowledge that this is a prerelease build of RedM, and I am aware my resources *will* become incompatible once RedM ships.'

name 'fw_crafting'
author 'Project Territory'
description 'Craft Rope from Plant Fiber'
version '1.0.0'

lua54 'yes'

dependencies {
    'fw_core',
    'fw_characters',
    'fw_inventory',
    'vorp_lib',
}

shared_scripts {
    '@vorp_lib/import.lua',
}

client_scripts {
    'client/main.lua',
}

server_scripts {
    'server/main.lua',
}

dependencies does not start those resources for you. It only stops fw_crafting from starting before them. The ensure order above still matters.

There is no fw_crafting database table. The recipe is just logic; the satchel that holds the items is already saved by fw_inventory. A resource that only moves items other resources already track does not need a table of its own.

docs.title: Add the ingredient
docs.text:
Rope already exists — it is in fw_inventory's own item list. Plant Fiber does not, so fw_crafting registers it with RegisterItem the first time it starts:

local itemOk, itemErr = exports.fw_inventory:RegisterItem({
    name = 'plant_fiber',
    label = 'Plant Fiber',
    category = 'materials',
    width = 1,
    height = 1,
    stack = 20,
    description = 'Stripped fiber from a yucca or similar plant. Good for cordage.',
})
if not itemOk then
    print('[fw_crafting] ' .. tostring(itemErr))
end

category has to be one already in use: ammo, animals, documents, food, herbs, horse, medical, tools, valuables, currency, weapons, materials, or container. Calling RegisterItem again on every restart is normal — it replaces the same definition, it does not fail on the second call.

This item has no image, so the satchel screen falls back to a blank tile. To give it a picture, drop a PNG named after the item, plant_fiber.png, into fw_inventory/images/. That is an asset, not a code change, so it does not touch anything fw_inventory owns in script.

docs.title: The recipe and the crafting logic
docs.text:
Keep recipes in a table, even with only one in it:

local RECIPES = {
    rope = {
        result = 'rope',
        resultCount = 1,
        ingredients = {
            plant_fiber = 3,
        },
    },
}

Crafting touches the satchel twice — take the ingredients, then add the result — and those are two separate calls to fw_inventory. Nothing stops a player from being one item short on the second call. Handle both directions:

  • Check every ingredient count before removing any of them. A recipe with two ingredients should never take the first and then fail on the second.
  • If adding the result fails — the satchel is full — give the ingredients back. The player should not lose materials for a craft that did not produce anything.
--- How many of name the player is carrying, from a GetItems snapshot.
---@param items table[]
---@param name string
---@return integer
local function countOf(items, name)
    local total = 0
    for index = 1, #items do
        if items[index].name == name then
            total = total + (items[index].count or 0)
        end
    end
    return total
end

--- Takes every ingredient for a recipe, or none of them.
---@param source integer
---@param recipe table
---@return boolean ok
---@return string|nil err
local function takeIngredients(source, recipe)
    local items, err = exports.fw_inventory:GetItems(source)
    if items == nil then
        return false, err
    end

    for name, needed in pairs(recipe.ingredients) do
        if countOf(items, name) < needed then
            return false, 'You do not have enough materials.'
        end
    end

    local taken = {}
    for name, needed in pairs(recipe.ingredients) do
        local ok, removeErr = exports.fw_inventory:RemoveItem(source, name, needed)
        if not ok then
            for takenName, takenCount in pairs(taken) do
                exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, takenName, takenCount)
            end
            return false, removeErr
        end
        taken[name] = needed
    end

    return true, nil
end

--- Runs one craft attempt. Ingredients come back if the result cannot fit.
---@param source integer
---@param recipeName string
---@return boolean ok
---@return string message
local function craft(source, recipeName)
    local recipe = RECIPES[recipeName]
    if recipe == nil then
        return false, 'That is not something you know how to make.'
    end

    local took, takeErr = takeIngredients(source, recipe)
    if not took then
        return false, takeErr or 'Could not take the materials.'
    end

    local added, addErr = exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, recipe.result, recipe.resultCount)
    if not added then
        for name, needed in pairs(recipe.ingredients) do
            exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(source, name, needed)
        end
        return false, addErr or 'Could not carry the result.'
    end

    return true, ('Crafted %d %s.'):format(recipe.resultCount, recipe.result)
end

GetItems and RemoveItem already say no when the player has no character selected, or does not hold enough — fw_crafting does not repeat those checks itself. Read the call before you copy it elsewhere; do not assume what it rejects.

docs.title: The server event
docs.text:
The client only ever sends a recipe name, never a count or an item. Counts come from the RECIPES table on the server, where the player cannot change them.

RegisterNetEvent('fw_crafting:craft', function(recipeName)
    local src = source

    if not ready then
        TriggerClientEvent('fw_crafting:result', src, false, 'Crafting is not ready yet.')
        return
    end

    local ok, message = craft(src, recipeName)
    TriggerClientEvent('fw_crafting:result', src, ok, message)
end)

local src = source reads the player number off the event itself, not off an argument. A TriggerServerEvent('fw_crafting:craft', recipeName) call cannot forge who it is — source is set by FXServer before your handler runs. If this line were instead a source argument the client passed in, any player could craft on behalf of any other player's inventory by sending someone else's number.

docs.title: The rest of server/main.lua
docs.text:
This is the same shape as every other fw_* resource: wait for what you depend on, register the item, check in, then say you are ready.

local Logger = Import('logger').Logger
local LOG_OPTIONS = { prefix = 'fw_crafting' }

local ready = false

local RECIPES = {
    rope = {
        result = 'rope',
        resultCount = 1,
        ingredients = {
            plant_fiber = 3,
        },
    },
}

local function log(message, level)
    if level == 'info' then
        Logger:Info(message, LOG_OPTIONS)
        return
    end
    Logger:Error(message, LOG_OPTIONS)
end

local function coreReady()
    local ok, isReady = pcall(function() return exports.fw_core:IsReady() end)
    return ok and isReady == true
end

local function charactersReady()
    local ok, isReady = pcall(function() return exports.fw_characters:IsReady() end)
    return ok and isReady == true
end

local function inventoryReady()
    local ok, isReady = pcall(function() return exports.fw_inventory:IsReady() end)
    return ok and isReady == true
end

-- countOf, takeIngredients, craft go here, as above

RegisterNetEvent('fw_crafting:craft', function(recipeName)
    -- as above
end)

--- Gives test materials from the server console, or to another player by number.
--- Not for players: RegisterCommand's third argument restricts it to an ace.
RegisterCommand('fw_crafting_give', function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1]) or source
    exports.fw_inventory:AddItem(target, 'plant_fiber', 10)
end, true)

local function waitUntil(check, label)
    if check() then
        return true
    end
    local timeoutAt = GetGameTimer() + 120000
    while not check() do
        if GetGameTimer() >= timeoutAt then
            log(label .. ' did not become ready')
            return false
        end
        Wait(100)
    end
    return true
end

if not waitUntil(coreReady, 'fw_core') then return end
if not waitUntil(charactersReady, 'fw_characters') then return end
if not waitUntil(inventoryReady, 'fw_inventory') then return end

local registered, registerErr = exports.fw_core:RegisterResource(1)
if not registered then
    log(registerErr or 'fw_core registration failed')
    return
end

local itemOk, itemErr = exports.fw_inventory:RegisterItem({
    name = 'plant_fiber',
    label = 'Plant Fiber',
    category = 'materials',
    width = 1,
    height = 1,
    stack = 20,
    description = 'Stripped fiber from a yucca or similar plant. Good for cordage.',
})
if not itemOk then
    log(itemErr or 'could not register plant_fiber')
end

ready = true
log('ready.', 'info')

fw_crafting_give is restricted the same way fw_core's own fw_health command is: the server console can always run it, and a player can only run it in-game if you grant the ace. Console is enough for testing. If you do want it in-game for admins, add this to permissions.cfg:

add_ace group.admin command.fw_crafting_give allow

fw_crafting keeps no state of its own between restarts — no table in memory keyed by player, nothing to walk on onResourceStop. When a resource only calls out to other resources and keeps nothing itself, there is nothing to clean up. That will not stay true once a resource tracks its own state, and fw_core's own onResourceStop handler, which forgets a resource's registration when it stops, is what that cleanup looks like.

docs.title: client/main.lua
docs.text:
The client sends the command and prints whatever the server decides happened. It does not touch items, and it does not decide whether the craft worked.

local Logger = Import('logger').Logger
local LOG_OPTIONS = { prefix = 'fw_crafting' }

--- Writes one line with vorp_lib on this player's game. level is error or info.
---@param message string
---@param level string|nil
---@return nil
local function say(message, level)
    if level == 'info' then
        Logger:Info(message, LOG_OPTIONS)
        return
    end
    Logger:Error(message, LOG_OPTIONS)
end

RegisterCommand('craft', function(_, args)
    local recipe = args[1] or 'rope'
    TriggerServerEvent('fw_crafting:craft', recipe)
end, false)

RegisterNetEvent('fw_crafting:result', function(ok, message)
    say(message, ok and 'info' or nil)
end)

This is the same say helper fw_trade uses for its own rejections. There is no on-screen toast in this framework yet — feedback is a line in the player's own F8 console. Match that instead of inventing a second way to talk to the player.

args[1] lets /craft rope name a recipe. With one recipe it is not load-bearing, but it means adding a second recipe to RECIPES does not also require a second command.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
ensure vorp_lib
ensure fw_core
ensure fw_characters
ensure fw_inventory
ensure fw_crafting

Start the server. The console should show:

[fw_core][info] ready version=1.1.0 api=1
[fw_characters][info] ready version=1.0.0
[fw_inventory] ready. 6 items.
[fw_crafting] ready.

In the server console, give yourself fiber and craft:

fw_crafting_give <your server id>

In the player's game, open the satchel and confirm 10 Plant Fiber are there, then type:

/craft

The console (F8) should print Crafted 1 Rope., and the satchel should show 7 Plant Fiber and 1 Rope. Typing /craft again with fewer than 3 Plant Fiber should print You do not have enough materials. and change nothing.

docs.title: Where to go from here
docs.text:
• More recipes are more entries in RECIPES. The crafting logic does not change.
  • Right now any player can type /craft from anywhere. A real crafting station would check distance to a prop, or an animation finishing, before calling craft. That check belongs on the server, next to the RECIPES lookup — not on the client, which can only ever be a suggestion.
  • A player crafting as fast as they can press Enter is not covered here. A small per-player cooldown, checked in the same place ready is checked, is the next thing to add before this goes near real players.
  • If the crafted item should do something when used — like dried_meat does in fw_inventory — register that separately with RegisterUsable. Crafting an item and using an item are two different calls.

docs.title: vorp_lib
docs.text:
Runs in the player's game. This page is the loading prompt, the revolver cylinder at the bottom right, a map blip, and copying a line to the clipboard. The game has one of these prompts. Starting it again only changes the words.

vorp_lib has to be started before the script that calls it.

docs.title: SpinnerStart
docs.text:
--- Shows the loading prompt. A string is the words. A table may also set how long it stays, in milliseconds.
--- No duration means it stays until SpinnerStop. Nothing comes back.
---@param data string|table|nil
---@return nil
exports.vorp_lib:SpinnerStart(data)

exports.vorp_lib:SpinnerStart('Opening')

exports.vorp_lib:SpinnerStart({ text = 'Opening', duration = 2000 })

text is the line next to the cylinder. duration is how many milliseconds until it goes away on its own. Leave duration out when your own code decides when it is finished, then call SpinnerStop.

docs.title: SpinnerStop
docs.text:
--- Hides the loading prompt.
---@return nil
exports.vorp_lib:SpinnerStop()

exports.vorp_lib:SpinnerStop()

Call this when the wait is over, including when the player cancels it. Stopping when nothing is showing is safe.

docs.title: copyToClipBoard
docs.text:
--- Copies one line onto the player's clipboard. Nothing comes back.
--- A value that is not text is ignored.
---@param text string
---@return nil
exports.vorp_lib:copyToClipBoard(text)

exports.vorp_lib:copyToClipBoard('vector4(-324.16, 803.62, 117.88, 272.93)')

Call this from the player's game. text is the exact line they can paste. The admin menu uses it when an admin copies where they are standing.

docs.title: Blips
docs.text:
A blip is a mark on the map. You create it from the player's game, in the resource that owns the place. Import loads the blip module from vorp_lib. vorp_lib has to be started first.

Options.card is the card that opens when the player hovers that blip on the map. Selecting the blip keeps the card open and writes footer on the line that usually names the town. Hovering does not change that line. A blip with no card is the same mark as before.

Options.range is how close the player must be, in metres, before a coords blip exists. Inside that distance the mark is created. It stays up until the player is 20 metres past it, so it does not flicker on the edge, and then it is removed. Walk back inside the range and it is created again, card included. Leave range out and the mark stays on the map. Range applies to a coords blip. An entity, area, or radius blip ignores it.

--- Puts a mark on the map. Options.card opens when the player hovers that mark.
--- The blip is what you keep. Call :Remove() on it when the place is gone.
---@param blipType string coords, entity, area, or radius
---@param params table the style, the place, and Options
---@return table blip
Blips:Create(blipType, params)

local module = Import({ 'blips' })
local Blips = module.Blips

Blips:Create('coords', {
    Blip = joaat('BLIP_STYLE_SHOP'),
    Pos = vector3(-324.16, 803.62, 117.88),
    Options = {
        name = 'General Store',
        sprite = joaat('blip_shop_store'),
        color = 'yellow',
        range = 120,
        card = {
            type = 'map_card_mission',
            title = 'General Store',
            subtitle = 'Valentine',
            description = 'Goods, bandages, and ammunition.',
            footer = 'Valentine, The Heartlands, NH',
            txd = 'map_card_val_generalstore',
            txn = 'image',
        },
    },
})

type has to be map_card_mission. Any other word is skipped, the blip still appears, and the player's console (F8) shows a warning. title is the large line. Leave it out and that line is empty. subtitle is the smaller line under the title. description is the body. ~n~ starts a new line in that body. footer is the region line after the player selects the blip. txd is the picture's texture dictionary, such as map_card_val_generalstore. Leave txd out and the card has no picture. txn is the texture name inside that dictionary. The store sample uses image.

Removing the blip closes its card. Restarting the resource does the same.
